regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): clear: where
regions.description: `$19:$18` := the PPU address of the cursor (`$84B1`), one row up (`$84A5`).

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): clear: the loop
regions.description: Fill tile `$14` := `$20` (blank), width `$15` := `$82A1+$51`, height `$17` := `$82A9+$51` rows: a run of blanks (`$C036`) per row, the address += `$20`. **This box is only a blank area - no frame is drawn.**

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): return
regions.description: `RTS`.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): fetch a character (`$83F3`)
regions.description: `JSR $C006` with `05 0E 80`: bank 5 `$800F` (the dialogue fetch, one character a call; `$15` = the current character).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $83F6
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 2 $83F3 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 5 $800F**. The stored word is $800E rather than $800F because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): 0: the end
regions.description: A character 0 sets the state `$83`.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): 1: a screenful
regions.description: Character 1 sets the state `$81`.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): `$0D`: a new line
regions.description: The column `$0608` := the box's column, the row `$05F0` += 1 and on to the next character in the same frame.

regions.name: Characters with a fixed tile
Their tiles
regions.description: `08 09 0C 0D 0E 0F`: font set 1.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): which tile? (`$8429`)
regions.description: The six characters `a e f i o t` (table `$841D`) take the fixed tiles `$08 $09 $0C $0D $0E $0F` of font set 1. Otherwise: **`$5C` and above (lowercase and the rest of the font) and `$3A-$3F` (the punctuation) get a NEW tile each time**; `$40-$5B` (`@`, A-Z and `[`... the full stop is `$5B`), `$30-$39` (digits), space and everything else are drawn directly as their own tile.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): a direct character
regions.description: Reserve 4 bytes (`$C039`); no room: `DEC $0638,X` (the fetch is taken back) and return, to try again next frame. Otherwise queue the tile (`$8482`), the column += 1 and fetch the next character in the same frame.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): after the tile
TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): a dynamic character
regions.description: Reserve 14 bytes; **tile `$0650` (from `$60`) gets the glyph: CHR address by `$827F`, the glyph by `$815D`**; the tile number is queued at the cursor (`$8482`), `$0650` += 1. RUN: the typed letters come out as tiles `$60, $61, $62 ...` and the CHR bytes at those tiles equal the font's glyphs.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): queue one tile (`$8482`)
regions.description: An item of count 1: PPU address of the cursor (`$84B1`) minus one row (`$84A5`), tile = `$15`.

regions.name: TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): one row up (`$84A5`)
TEXT BOX / DIALOGUE (type `$34`, bank 2 `$82C0`, slot `$8009`; X = the object): cursor to PPU address (`$84B1`)
regions.description: `$2000 + 32 x row + column` from `$05F0` and `$0608` into `$19:$18` (nametable 0 only).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): first frame?
regions.description: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): type bit 7 set goes to the per-frame code (`$8543`). Table stats: `$31` and `$32` flags `$6A`, hit points 4, attack 1, death types `$B1` / `$B2`; `$33` flags `$6A`, no hit points; `$35` is the screen object (bank 5).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): set-up
regions.description: `$0668` (the OPENED flag) := 0 and `$07B8` (the mode) := 0; metasprite `$0548` := `$31`.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): a box?
regions.description: Type `$31`?

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): the mode
regions.description: Mode 1 for a box in a labyrinth room; mode 2 when `$30` bit 5 or 6 is set (a special screen or a corridor: a gate's reward). Shop items stay mode 0.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): the item
regions.description: `$0680,X` := `$55`, the item id of the room (`$A377[sub-id]`, or `$EF40[corridor]` for a gate). A shop item has its id from the shop table instead.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): a shop item?
regions.description: Type `$33`?

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): shop item: its price on the floor
regions.description: `$07A0` (the sold flag) := 0; `JSR $C0AE`; the price `$0770 : $0758` is printed by `JSR $C04E` (`$E24B`) at the PPU address of the object's tile (`$05D8 : $05C0` + `$3F`): the number appears under the item. Then straight to the opened state (`$855E`). RUN: shop 1's items showed 1000 under each.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): box: wait for the other box
regions.description: `$56` is the id of the box that is open. Another box open (not `$FF`, not this id): an id of `$14` or more (a drop) does not wait, a real item does - the object returns until the other is taken. So only one item box is open at a time.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): box: mode 2 opens at once
regions.description: A gate's reward (mode 2) becomes type `$B1` and goes straight to the open state. RUN: the box in the cleared gate was open on its first frame.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): box: the stats
regions.description: `JSR $C0AE`: hit points 4.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): every frame: the scroll
regions.description: `JSR $C12C`: in a corridor the object slides with the scroll; carry (off the bottom) removes it.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): already open?
regions.description: `$0668` non-zero goes to the collecting code `$85DE`.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): closed: shoot it open
regions.description: Hit points 0 open it. Otherwise `JSR $C0CF` (`$D29F`, hit test, mask `$20`) and `JMP $C0D2` (`$D2BB`): the shots take its 4 hit points down; at 0 the death type `$B1` (the same type again) arrives with 0 hit points. RUN: touching the closed box did nothing.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): OPEN
regions.description: `$0668` := 1, metasprite `$25`; `JSR $880C`: an item id of `$14` or more is a drop (carry set), under that a real item (`$858E`).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): a drop is shown as a tile
regions.description: A drop (item 20, 21, 22 from an enemy's box) draws its picture as background tiles `$858B[id - 20]` (`2C 24 28`) at the object's cell through `$8812` (the block-break routine with that tile, class 0).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): position helper
regions.description: `$19 : $18 : $17` := x, y, 0 (the arguments of `$FA96`). RTS.

regions.name: Drop pictures: indexed by the item id - 20
regions.description: `0C 0B 01 | 2C 24 28`: read at `$8577 + id`; only ids 20-22 (`$858B-$858D` = `2C 24 28`) occur; the first three bytes are never read.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): a real item: shop item or box?
regions.description: Type `$B3`: a shop item.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): shop item: where the icon goes
regions.description: `$19 : $18` := `$100 + 16 x $0698`: the PPU address of the tile number the shop gave the item (`$5C`, `$D8`, `$DC`). (`$0698` is the item's icon tile.)

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): box: where the icon goes
regions.description: `$19 : $18` := `$15C0` (tile `$5C`) and `$56` := the item id: this box is now the open one.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): upload the icon
regions.description: `JSR $81B2` (slot `$8003` in this bank): icon A of the 18 at `$8E0C` is written to the CHR address. RUN: the opened box's picture appeared in tiles `$5C-$5F`.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): mode 2: no cell picture
regions.description: Mode 2 (a gate's reward) skips the picture and goes to collecting.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): show the item in its cell
regions.description: The cell gets the icon's tiles (`$0698` for a shop item, `$5C` for a box) through `$8812` and `$FA96` (class 0, so the ship can walk onto it).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): collecting: a shop item?
regions.description: Only type `$B3` buys; others go to `$861C`.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): shop item: sold out
regions.description: `$07A0` non-zero (set by the shop's screen object when another item was bought): the cell turns to floor (tile `$1C`) and the item is removed. RUN: with one item bought the other two became floor within 14 frames.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): shop item: touched?
regions.description: `JSR $C0C3`: carry set when the ship touches it.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): shop item: can the player pay?
regions.description: The chips `$4D : $4C` minus the price `$0770 : $0758`; borrow returns (not enough).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): return
regions.description: RTS.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): shop item: pay
regions.description: The chips become the difference; `$FCE7` with A = 0 redraws the counter and re-derives the gun tier; then collect. RUN: chips 4095 -> 3095 for a price of 1000.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): box: touched?
regions.description: `JSR $C0C3`; carry clear returns.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): collect
regions.description: An id under `$14` clears `$56` ($FF): the box is no longer the open one.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): collect: the cell becomes floor
regions.description: Unless mode 2: tile `$1C`, class 0 (`$FA96`-family `$C11A`).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): collect: which mode
regions.description: Mode 0 (a shop item) applies the item; mode 1 sets the item flag; mode 2 does the gate.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): mode 2: the gate's reward
regions.description: Sparks at x `$50` and `$90` (bank 1 `$8003` through `$8817`), then a far call (inline `01 05 80`) to bank 1 `$8006` with A = `$10`, Y = `$FF`, `$19` = `$70`, `$18` = `$60`. RUN: sparks at x 80 and 144, and breaks at the door cells.

regions.name: Far-call argument at $8663
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 2 $8660 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 1 $8006**. The stored word is $8005 rather than $8006 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): mode 2: on to the doors
ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): mode 1: remember it
regions.description: `JSR $C066` (`$EFE9`): the item flag `$5E` (the room's sub-id) is set, so the box does not come back. RUN: the flag array gained the room's bit.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): the door cells: scan
regions.description: Eight records of 4 bytes at `$87EC` ([cell][new class][attribute][opening mask]): the class under the cell must be 14.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): the door cells: change
regions.description: If the room's opening bit (`$54 AND mask`) is set, the cell gets the picture `$14` with the record's class and attribute through `$8812`. **In a cleared gate the 'open door' cell (metatile `$0C`, class 14) becomes class 10, the cover that takes four shots, and the outer cell class 8** - so the reward opens the way to the warp panel. RUN: in corridor 5's gate the cell (7, 2) went from class 14 to 10 when the reward was taken. Class 14 occurs nowhere else in the map's rooms (checked for every ordinary room).

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): the door cells: next
regions.description: X += 4 until `$20`.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): apply the item
regions.description: `LDA $0680,X / JSR $86BC`: the effect of the item (see the pick-up effects). RUN: item 20 gave +40 life; the shop's item 20 +40.

regions.name: ITEM OBJECTS (bank 2 slot `$800F`, reached from bank 6 `$99F1` for types `$31` box, `$32` and `$33` shop item; X = the object): remove the object
regions.description: `PLA / TAX / JMP $C048`.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item < 11?
regions.description: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item ids 0-10 are the eleven upgradable weapons (weapon = id + 1, the icon numbers of the status screen); 11 is the Enemy Eraser; 12-17 are the six power-ups; 18 and over are the item-box drops. `$10` := the id; 11 or more branches to `$8711`.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): weapon: which level byte
regions.description: Y := id / 4 (the byte `$04AC + Y`), X := id mod 4 (the pair of bits): the 11 weapons' levels are two bits each in `$04AC-$04AE`.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): weapon: already at level 3?
regions.description: The byte AND the mask `$87C6[X]` equal to the mask means both bits set: level 3.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): weapon at level 3: chips instead
regions.description: `$4D` (the chip count's high byte) += 7 (so +1,792 chips, capped at CHIP MAX), capped at `$FF`, and a chip add of 0 with sound `$D4`-argument through `$C12F` (`$FCE7`, which redraws and re-derives the gun tier). RUN: items 0, 3 and 10 with all weapons at level 3 filled the chips from 100 to CHIP MAX (500 in the run: the add is capped).

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): weapon: one level up
PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): weapon: the chips redraw, and the sprite tiles
regions.description: A chip add of 0 (`$FCE7`: redraw the counter, set the gun tier); if the id + 1 equals the selected weapon `$3C`, `JSR $C069` (`$F726`) reloads that weapon's sprite tiles for the new level.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): sound
regions.description: Sound `$35` (the weapon / upgrade jingle).

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): +16 life
regions.description: `A := $10`, `JMP $C00C` (`$FD67`, add A to the life). **Every upgrade gives 16 life.** RUN: life 32 -> 48 for ids 0-11, 14-16, 21.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): return
regions.description: RTS.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 11: the Enemy Eraser
regions.description: `$04AE` bit 6 set (the Eraser is owned) and `$04AF` (its stock) += 20, capped at `$FF`, then the weapon ending `$86F3`. RUN: stock 3 -> 23 and `$04AE` 21 -> 85.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): items 12 and up: sound
regions.description: A is Y. The sound `$87BB[id - 12]` (`32 00 35 35 35 31 00 00 30 34 33`) is played when non-zero; ids under 13 take the life refill.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 12: Energy Tank icon - full life
regions.description: `$48` := `$47`: life becomes the maximum. No +16. RUN: 32 -> 128.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 13: Blue Lander - the Energy Tank effect
regions.description: `JSR $C033` (`$DF8C`, the score-bonus award: chips refilled to CHIP MAX, max life +8, life full, song `$31`) then +16 life. RUN: max life 128 -> 136, life 32 -> 136, chips 100 -> 500.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 14: Gun - attack +1
PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 15: Shield - shield +1
regions.description: `$4B` += 1 when it is not 0 (a zero shield stays 0).

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): attack / shield tail
regions.description: `JSR $C132` (`$FD0E`: the attack is capped at 4 and the player's attack `$05A8` is looked up in `$FD4B`) then +16 life. RUN: attack 1 -> 2, shield 1 -> 2.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 16: Consecutive Firing - fire rate +1
regions.description: `$6B` += 1, capped at 5; `JSR $882E` loads the shot delay `$39` := `$87CE[$6B]` (`0C 05 04 03 02 01`); +16 life. RUN: 1 -> 2.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 17: Red Lander - chip capacity +1
regions.description: `$46` += 1 (capped at 10); `JSR $8820` takes CHIP MAX `$4E/$4F` from `$87D4[level]` (50, 100, 150, 200, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400, 4000, 6000, 30000); the chips and the life are filled to their maxima. RUN: level 1 -> 2, CHIP MAX 500 -> 150, chips 100 -> 150, life 32 -> 128 (no +16).

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): items 18-20: +40 life
regions.description: Under 21: `LDA #$28 / JSR $C00C`: life += 40, no +16. Item 20 also plays sound `$30` from the table. RUN: ids 18, 19, 20 gave +40.

regions.name: PICK-UP EFFECTS (bank 2 slot `$8015` -> `$86BC`; A = the item id; also reached from the shop and the reward screens): item 21: 500 chips
regions.description: `$4D` += 1 (+256) and `$FCE7` with A = `$F4` (+244): +500 chips, capped at CHIP MAX; then +16 life. RUN: chips 100 -> 500 (the cap), life +16, sound `$34`.

regions.name: The font: 45 glyphs, 1bpp, 7 bytes each
regions.description: 315 bytes = 45 x 7, and the seven is the whole point. This block is NOT tile-shaped and no graphics test that assumes 16 bytes per tile can see it - which is why this project's scan for a 1bpp font stored as 2bpp, sixteen consecutive tiles with an all-zero second bit plane, came back empty across the entire ROM. Playbook section 7 names this exact case: when a block will not divide by 16, ask what expands it before deciding it is not graphics. THE EXPANDER is bank 2 $806C. Per glyph it reserves a 19-byte queue entry, writes a count of $10 and the destination, then copies seven source bytes into data bytes 0-6, zeroes byte 7 at $8098, and zeroes bytes 8-15 through STA $010B,X - so the glyph occupies rows 0-6 of the low bit plane, row 7 is blank and the high plane is empty. It then advances the destination by $10 and the source by SEVEN, at $80AB. Every glyph therefore uses colour 1 only. CONFIRMED AGAINST THE HARDWARE: expanding the 41 glyphs this ROM's own record table uploads and comparing them with the live CHR RAM in a title-screen savestate gives 41 matches out of 41, byte for byte. The remaining four glyphs in the block are not uploaded by that table.

regions.name: The font, continued: 31 more 7-byte glyphs
regions.description: The rest of the 1bpp, seven-bytes-a-glyph font that begins at $8BF8, expanded by the same routine, $806C: !, a double quote, two dots (the umlaut drawn above the password grid's lowercase rows), an apostrophe, a-z, and a slashed zero. Named by the second and third upload-record sets at $810B and $8134; the highest byte any record reads is $8E0B, the byte before the item icons at $8E0C, which is the extent. HARDWARE: set 2 puts these on the password screen - 32 of 32 glyphs match that savestate's live CHR (a-z at tiles $81-$9A, ! at $9B, the dots at $AE, the slashed zero over '0' at $30) - and set 1's eight glyphs match a labyrinth savestate 8 of 8. Records address sources byte-wise, not only on a 7-byte grid: set 1 reads from $8D3D.

regions.name: Item icons: 18 x 2x2 tiles, raw 2bpp
regions.description: Eighteen 16x16 icons, 64 bytes each = four ordinary 2bpp tiles, stored UNCOMPRESSED. THE UPLOADER is bank 2 $81B2 (entry slot $8003): source = $8E0C + A * $40, queued as two 32-byte PPU writes to the CHR address in $18/$19. The four tiles are column-major - the status screen's $86F4 draws a selected icon as tiles $3C $3E over $3D $3F. THE EXTENT: the highest index any caller passes is 17 ($11, in bank 3's reward table $817A), and $8E0C + 18 * 64 is $928C, exactly where the next table - read by the other uploader - begins. Indices 0-11 are the twelve weapons: the status screen's $84CB uploads 0-11 to $1800-$1AFF (tiles $80-$AF) and $86ED uploads the selected one, index $3C - 1, to tile $3C. Indices 12-17 are non-weapon items, appearing only in the reward table. Rendered, all eighteen are recognisable framed pictures (docs/graphics.html). WHICH ICON IS WHICH WEAPON by name is not established from the ROM.

regions.name: Key icons: the shared high bit plane
regions.description: The high bit planes of all eight key icons - one 2x2 frame every key shares. Bank 2 $8212 (entry slot $8006) builds each tile from 8 low-plane bytes out of the icon ($92AC + 32k) and 8 high-plane bytes from here: $928C,Y for tiles 0 and 2 and $9294,Y for tiles 1 and 3, with Y running 0-7 and then $10-$17. Those four reads cover $928C-$92AB exactly, 32 bytes. CORRECTION: tools/find-tables.py claimed $928C-$9293 as a bare 8-byte table; it is a quarter of this plane.

regions.name: Key icons: 8 x 32 bytes of low bit plane
regions.description: Eight 16x16 icons stored as the LOW bit plane only, 32 bytes each (four tiles x 8 rows); the high plane is shared, at $928C. Uploader bank 2 $8212: source = $92AC + A * 32. Index 0 is an empty frame. THE EXTENT: callers pass 0-7 - bank 7 $ED51 passes $0058,Y AND $0F with 8 excluded, the status screen passes 1-7, and $F547 passes a per-area value from $F6DA - and $92AC + 8 * 32 is $93AC, where the unclaimed gap ends. Indices 1-7 are the SEVEN KEYS: $F547 ORs bit (k - 1) into $04B0 when key k is collected, and the status screen draws key k's icon only when that bit is set.

The decoder is $DB52, run from NMI a budgeted number of bytes per frame after $D7F9 arms it. Decoding starts in literal mode, the escape toggles into a run section of [value][count] pairs (count 0 = 256), the escape toggles back, and two escape bytes in a row end the block. regions.name: Fill: 16 x $FF
regions.description: 16 bytes of $FF running from the end of the bank's last claimed structure to $BFFE, the byte before the bank-identity byte at $BFFF that the reset path checks. No reader.

regions.name: Bank 2 identity byte
regions.description: One byte at $BFFF, the last byte of PRG bank 2, holding the bank's own number. Banks 0 to 6 each carry one; bank 7 does not, because bank 7's last byte is at $FFFF and belongs to the IRQ vector. These seven bytes are the ROM half of a boot-time mapper self-test. $FF23-$FF43, reached from the reset handler, is a loop over Y = 6 down to 0: TYA / JSR $D705 selects the bank in Y, CPY $BFFF then compares Y against the byte this region holds, and BEQ $FF41 falls through to DEY only when the two agree. If they do not, LDA $FF3A,Y fetches a per-bank code, stores it at $0180, calls $DED2 and then spins forever at JMP $FF37. So the game refuses to start unless every one of the seven switchable banks can be selected and answers with its own number - which is the check a UxROM board needs, because a bus conflict on the latch fails silently and leaves the wrong bank mapped. Reading the byte at $BFFF works no matter which bank is live precisely because every bank has one at the same address and they all differ. NOT ESTABLISHED: what $DED2 does with $0180, and therefore whether the failure is displayed or merely hangs.

regions.name: Inline argument at $82BD
regions.description: 4 bytes of inline argument data following `JSR $D5CC` at bank 3 $82BA - four-byte inline argument. The callee pops its own return address and reads these bytes through it, so they are data that happens to sit in the instruction stream, and a trace that decodes them produces nonsense that still looks like code. The length is not a guess: it is the constant the callee advances its own pointer by. What the bytes MEAN is not claimed. See annotations/dispatch.json for the routine and for how the class of these routines was enumerated.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): PPU control
regions.description: `$FF` := (`$FF` OR 8) AND `$DF`: 8 x 8 sprites from pattern table 1, and written to PPUCTRL.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): the font tiles
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$1010`; `LDA #$03 / LDY #$02 / JSR $C42` (`$D7F9`): bank 2 block 3 (the 15 map-quadrant tiles) armed for CHR `$1010`; then a far call bank 2 `$8012` (`02 11 80`): the font loader of bank 2 (probably set 2, the password screen's a-z, !, ?, umlaut dots and slashed zero; not isolated).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $82DC
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 3 $82D9 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 2 $8012**. The stored word is $8011 rather than $8012 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): draw the grid
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$2284`, X := 22, Y := 5: `JSR $8BB3`; then `JSR $8B7E`; sound `$19` (the password-screen music) and return.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): wait for a button (`$82F6`)
regions.description: `JSR $C0E4`; a new A, B, Select or Start (`AND #$F0`) is needed, then `JMP $8B7E`.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): valid
regions.description: `$2F` non-zero: `JSR $8473` applies the decoded state; `JMP $8397`.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): entry: show the password (slot `$8009`)

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): clear the field
PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): edit loop: finished?
regions.description: `JSR $8711`; zero leaves.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): edit loop: mode
PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): edit loop: draw the cursor
regions.description: `JSR $8B7E`.

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): edit loop: input
regions.description: `JSR $887F`: carry set (a button other than the grid) goes to `$838E` (`JSR $87B5`), otherwise `JSR $87F2` (a character chosen).

regions.name: PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): edit loop: wait
PASSWORD SCREEN, entry and flow (bank 3): leave the screen (`$8397`)
regions.description: Sprites hidden, sound `$1F`, the fade out (`$C0ED`), PPUCTRL restored (`$FF` AND `$F7`, OR `$20`: 8 x 16 sprites): `RTS`.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): copy the state
regions.description: `$0438 + Y` := `$049F + Y`, Y = 17..1: **index i (0-16) = the byte `$04A0 + i`** (the item flags `$04A0-$04A8`, the corridor-cleared flags `$04A9-$04AB`, the weapon levels `$04AC-$04AE`, the Eraser stock `$04AF`, the keys `$04B0`) lands at `$0439 + i`.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): chip level in byte 8
regions.description: The chip level `$46` is shifted bit by bit into `$0441` (the copy of `$04A8`) from the bottom, four times: **`$04A8` keeps only its low nibble (item flags 64-67), moved up; the chip level takes the bottom nibble reversed.**

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): byte 14
regions.description: `$0447` (the copy of `$04AE`) AND `$7F`: **bit 7 is not saved** (the Eraser flag bit 6 is).

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): max life and fire rate (byte 17)
regions.description: `$044A` := `$47` (0 if it is `$FF`) OR `$6B`: the max life in the high five bits (**only its multiples of 8 survive**) and the fire rate `$6B` (0-5) in the low three.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): column and attack (byte 18)
regions.description: `$044B` := (`$52` x 8) OR the three bits of (`$4A` - 1), reversed (`$8430`).

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): row and shield (byte 19)
regions.description: `$044C` := (`$53` x 8) OR the three bits of `$4B`, reversed.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): the score, first half (byte 20)
regions.description: The first three score digits `$0170-$0172` as one number 0-999 (`$844D`): the low byte to `$044D`, the top two bits shifted into `$0444` (the copy of `$04AB`) from the bottom.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): the score, second half (byte 21)
regions.description: `$0173-$0175` the same: `$044E` and two more bits into `$0444`. **`$04AB` (the corridor flags 17-21) therefore keeps only its low nibble, moved up: the cleared flag of corridor 21 (bit 4) is NOT in the password.** RUN: 300 random states through the ROM's own encoder and decoder came back exactly (apart from the dropped bits above), and `$04AB` = `$10` came back 0.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): insert three bits (`$8430`)
regions.description: `$10` := A; then the low three bits of Y are shifted into `$10` from the bottom (`$8439`): `$10` = A x 8 + reverse3(Y); returns A := `$10`.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): shift three bits in (`$8439`)
regions.description: Three times `LSR A / ROL $10`.

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): extract three bits (`$8443`)
regions.description: `$10` := 0; `JSR $8439`; Y := `$10`: A is shifted right three bits and Y gets those three bits reversed.

regions.name: PASSWORD ENCODER (`$83AE`): three digits to a number (`$844D`)
regions.description: A = the last digit, `$18` = the middle, `$19` = the first: **A (low) and `$18` (high) := 100 x `$19` + 10 x `$18` + A**.

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): copy back
regions.description: `$049F + Y` := `$0438 + Y`, Y = 17..1 (the reverse of the encoder's copy).

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): clear unsaved bits
PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): chip level
regions.description: Four times `LSR $04A8 / ROL A`: **`$46` := the chip level**, and `$04A8` loses those four bits (its saved nibble moves back down).

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): fire rate and max life
PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): column and attack
regions.description: `$044B` is split by `$8443`: `$7C` := the column, `$4A` := the three bits + 1.

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): row and shield
regions.description: `$044C`: `$7D` := the row, `$4B` := the three bits. **The position goes into `$7C/$7D` (the progress record), not `$52/$53`.**

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): the score, second half
regions.description: `$04AB`'s bottom two bits (shifted out) and `$044E` give `$0173-$0175` (`$8502`).

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): the score, first half
regions.description: The next two bits of `$04AB` and `$044D` give `$0170-$0172`. After the two halves `$04AB` has lost its four top bits' worth: it holds the corridor flags 17-20.

regions.name: PASSWORD APPLY (`$8473`): a number to three digits (`$8502`)
regions.description: A (low) and Y (high): `$C10E` (`$F9BA`) divides by 100 (hundreds digit -> `$19`), `$C10B` (`$F9AE`) divides the rest by 10: A := tens, Y := ones.

regions.name: The TGL password constant
regions.description: Three bytes, $13 $06 $0B. Those are grid indices, not ASCII: the password entry grid is A-Z then 0-9 read left to right and top to bottom, $88F2 stores a character as its grid index with LDA $16 / STA $0411,X, so A is 0 - and 19, 6, 11 is T, G, L. The on-screen grid in a password-screen savestate confirms the layout row by row. READ BY $857C: LDA $8513,Y / CMP $0411,Y for Y = 0,1,2, after which $8589 requires every character from index 3 to $1F to be zero. On a match $8592 sets $2F = 0 and $30 = 2 and returns with carry clear, SKIPPING THE CHECKSUM at $859B entirely. $30 is the game-mode byte. Bounded by its reader's operand and by the code either side: $8512 is an RTS and $8516 is a traced instruction start, so these three bytes are exactly the gap between. A CONSEQUENCE OF THE ENCODING, stated because the code says so and not because it was tried: a blank and the letter A are both the byte 0 - the savestate shows an untouched field is all $00 - so 'TGL' followed by any number of A's is the same 32 bytes as 'TGL' followed by blanks, and this check cannot tell them apart.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): wait
regions.description: `JSR $C045`: wait for the tile decompressor (the staging area `$0100-$011D` is about to be used).

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): the seed
regions.description: `$19` := (`$042F` >> 4) OR (`$0430` << 2), + `$1D`: **byte 23 of the stream, held in the last two characters, plus 29**.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): set-up
regions.description: `$17` (output index), `$14` (input offset), `$18` (mismatch count) := 0; `$16` := 8 groups.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): a group
regions.description: `LDX $14 / JSR $85BB`: four characters -> three bytes in `$0403-$0405`; X := the output index.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): a byte
regions.description: `LDA $0403,Y`; **index 23 (X = `$17`) is not XORed; every other byte is XORed with the seed, which then decrements.**

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): store and compare
regions.description: `$011E + X` := the byte; compared with the state buffer `$0439 + X`; a difference counts in `$18`.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): next
regions.description: Three bytes a group; the input offset += 4; eight groups. RUN: the group loop gave the encoder's bytes back.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): which mode?
regions.description: `$0400` zero (the check mode of `$8376`) goes to `$8574`; non-zero (entering a password) to the back door at `$857A`.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): check mode: the same as the game's own?
regions.description: No mismatches in `$18`: carry clear, accepted; any: `SEC`. **RUN: the password built from a state is accepted against that state and refused after one change (attack 2 -> 3).**

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): refused
regions.description: `SEC / RTS`.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): the TGL back door
regions.description: The first three characters against `$8513` (`13 06 0B`: T, G, L) and **every other of the 32 characters zero**: `$2F` := 0, `$30` := 2 (a TGL game), carry clear - **the checksum is skipped**. RUN: `T G L` + 29 blanks was accepted (`$30` = 2, `$2F` = 0); the same with one stray character in the last place was refused.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): the checksum
regions.description: The sum with the carries chained (`ADC`, no `CLC` in the loop) of the 22 bytes `$011E-$0133` (indices 0-21), plus index 23 (`$0135`, the raw seed byte), compared with index 22 (`$0134`): unequal refuses.

regions.name: PASSWORD DECODER (`$8516`; called by the editor `$887F` when 32 characters are entered): accepted: the state
regions.description: The 24 bytes `$011E-$0135` are copied to `$0439-$0450`; `CLC / RTS`. RUN: 60 random states built by `$83AE` / `$860E` were accepted and came back equal; a changed character in each was refused (60 of 60).

regions.name: PASSWORD UNPACK (`$85BB`): four characters
regions.description: Four characters from `$0411 + X` to `$0403-$0406`; the first three AND `$3F`.

regions.name: PASSWORD UNPACK (`$85BB`): byte 0
regions.description: `$0403` := char 0 OR (char 1 low two bits << 6).

regions.name: PASSWORD UNPACK (`$85BB`): byte 1
regions.description: `$0404` := (char 1 >> 2) OR (char 2 low four bits << 4).

regions.name: PASSWORD UNPACK (`$85BB`): byte 2
regions.description: `$0405` := (char 2 >> 4) OR (char 3 << 2); `RTS`. **The standard 6-bit unpack, four characters into three bytes.**

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): a seed
regions.description: `$0450` := a random byte (`$C0EA`); wait for the decompressor.

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): the checksum
regions.description: `$044F` := the carry-chained sum of `$0439-$044E` (indices 0-21) + the seed.

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): the encryption
regions.description: X = 30..1: `$00FF + X` := `$0438 + X` XOR the seed, the seed incrementing: **index k is XORed with seed + 29 - k**, which is what the decoder's decrementing seed (byte 23 + 29) undoes.

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): the seed in the clear
regions.description: `$0117` (index 23) := the seed itself.

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): 32 characters
regions.description: For each of the 32 characters `JSR $8654` and store it in `$0411 + Y`.

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): return
regions.description: `RTS`.

regions.name: PASSWORD BUILD (`$860E`): the next 6 bits (`$8654`)
regions.description: The 24 bytes `$0100-$0118` are one long shift register: six times `ROR` through all of them (X = 24..1) collecting the bits that fall out in A; A >> 2 is the character (0-63).

regions.name: PASSWORD FIELD DRAWING (`$866B`): draw the field
PASSWORD FIELD DRAWING (`$866B`): return
regions.description: `RTS`.

regions.name: PASSWORD FIELD DRAWING (`$866B`): where character X goes (`$8681`)
regions.description: X under 16 is the first row, otherwise the second (Y = 1: +`$40`) and X - 16; then X + 1 for each group of four passed (at 4, 8, 12): **the characters are shown in four groups of four with a blank between them, 16 + 3 columns, two rows.**

regions.name: PASSWORD FIELD DRAWING (`$866B`): draw one character (`$86A8`)
regions.description: A 5-byte PPU queue item (`JSR $C04B`, `JSR $C03C`): `$82` (a run of 2 with the address increment 32: a vertical pair), the address (`$18` + column, + `$40` per row), then the two tiles: the top `$20` (blank), or `$AE` for the lowercase letters (their umlaut dots), and the glyph:

regions.name: PASSWORD FIELD DRAWING (`$866B`): the glyph
regions.description: A character 0-25 is `A`-`Z` (+`$41`); 26-29 `0`-`3` (+`$16`); 30-55 the lowercase letters (+`$63`: tiles `$81-$9A`, with the dots `$AE` above); 56-61 `4`-`9` (-4); 62 and 63 the tiles `$9B` and `$9C` (`!` and `?`).

regions.name: PASSWORD FIELD DRAWING (`$866B`): store the tiles
regions.description: `$0104` := the glyph, `$0103` := Y (the top tile); `LDX $13`; `JMP $C03F` (`$D6F7`: the item is complete).

regions.name: Check menu cursor start (sprite 1)
regions.description: `54 00 00 50`: y, tile, attribute, x.

regions.name: PASSWORD CHECK MENU (`$8711`, called by `$832D`'s screen): draw the menu
regions.description: A window (`JSR $8BB3`, X = 14, Y = 7) at PPU `$20E8`, then the inline strings **GO OUT** at `$214B` and **WORD CHECK** at `$218B`;

regions.name: PASSWORD CHECK MENU (`$8711`, called by `$832D`'s screen): GO OUT
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`;

regions.name: "GO OUT" at $8723
regions.description: A queued PPU write item, written inline after `JSR $D576` at bank 3 $8720. Its shape is [count][ppu_hi][ppu_lo][count characters]: the destination $214B is in the block itself. The block is 9 bytes and the caller resumes immediately after it; the length comes from the first byte by the rule in $D591 - (byte & $7F) + 3 below $C0, 9 at or above - and $D5A5 advances the routine's own pointer by exactly that. It reads "GO OUT". Characters are ASCII for the letters and space. NOT ESTABLISHED: the glyphs for codes outside A-Z and space, which only the font can settle - and no font has been found yet, because CHR is RAM on this cartridge.

regions.name: PASSWORD CHECK MENU (`$8711`, called by `$832D`'s screen): WORD CHECK

regions.name: "WORD CHECK" at $872F

regions.name: PASSWORD CHECK MENU (`$8711`, called by `$832D`'s screen): loop: flicker
PASSWORD CHECK MENU (`$8711`, called by `$832D`'s screen): loop: Down, Up or Select
regions.description: `JSR $C0E4` (the new presses): bits 2, 3, 5 go to `$875D`.

regions.description: `LDA $0204 / CMP #$54 / RTS`. The callers (`$8347`, `$8379`) leave on Z.

regions.name: Unreferenced entry: clear nametable rows 0-19 ($C084), then $8B7E
regions.description: LDA #$20 / STA $15 / LDA #$20 / STA $14 / LDA #$00 / STA $17 / LDA #$14 / STA $16 / JSR $C084 ($E453), then falls into $8B7E. $8B7E has callers of its own (JSR at $82EE, $8380 and $87B5, JMP at $82FD); nothing names $8B6B, and the pairs $6B 8B / $6A 8B occur nowhere. It follows an RTS, so it is not a fall-through either. A LEAD. CORRECTION: the name said 'a 32 x 32 area at $1400'. $E453 clears rows `$17` to `$16` - 1 with fill `$14` (page `$15` only gives the first row's address): here rows 0-19 of the nametable at `$2000` with blanks `$20`, which is the area the opening box animation (`$8B7E`) then draws its frame in (the final frame is rows 3-19). The whole ROM was scanned again for `JSR`/`JMP $8B6B` and for the far-call spelling `03 6B 8B`: still nothing, so it stays a lead.

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): hide the cursors, set the first box (`$8B7E`)
WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): draw a frame
regions.description: `JSR $8BB3` with A = `$6C` (non-zero: draw the frame tiles). A frame of Y = 15 or more ends the routine, **so the last frame stays**.

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): erase it
regions.description: `JSR $8BB3` with A = 0: the same frame redrawn in blank tiles (`$20`) - **only the frame's own tiles are blanked, the inside is never touched**. The next, bigger frame is queued behind it.

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): grow
regions.description: Y := 1 if it was 0, else Y + 2 (Y runs 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15); X += 2 (X runs 6, 8 ... 22); the address -= `$21` (one row up, one column left; `BNE` is always taken as `$19` stays non-zero). **Eight steps from a box 8 x 2 at row 11 to one 24 x 17 at `$2064` (row 3, column 4).** RUN: it returns after 16 frames with the queue still holding the last row; the frame's bounding box goes rows 10-10 -> 8-14 -> 6-16 -> 4-17 -> 3-19 and columns 11-20 -> 4-27, and the final nametable is the frame of 24 x 17 tiles around the grid (the characters start at PPU `$2086`, row 4 column 6).

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): return
regions.description: `RTS`.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): draw or blank a frame
regions.description: Entry: `$19:$18` = the PPU address of its top-left tile, **X = the inner width, Y = the inner height**, A = 0 for a blank frame (`$1B`; `$8C76` then returns `$20` for every tile), any other value for the real tiles. The frame is (X + 2) x (Y + 2) tiles and **nothing inside it is drawn**. RUN: X = 4, Y = 2 gave rows `07 03 03 03 03 0B / 05 .. 0A / 05 .. 0A / 0D 0C 0C 0C 0C 0E`; X = 0, Y = 1 gave `07 0B / 05 0A / 0D 0E`. The top-left corner (tile `$07`) is queued first.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): top edge
regions.description: `$15` := X; if X is non-zero, `$18`++ and a run of X tiles `$03` along the row (`JSR $C036` = `$D5F8`: a PPU queue run with count `$15`, tile `$14`; bit 7 of the count = increment 32), `$18`--.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): top-right corner
regions.description: The left address is saved, `$18` += X + 1 (the `SEC` before `ADC`), and tile `$0B` is queued; then `$19` is saved too.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): side edges, if Y is non-zero
regions.description: `$15` := Y OR `$80` (a vertical run of Y), one row down (`JSR $C0E7` = `$DA1D`: the address + `$20`, wrapping past the nametable), tile `$0A` down the right side; then the left address is restored, one row down again and Y tiles `$05` down the left side.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): bottom row
regions.description: The left address is restored and saved again; for Y non-zero `$15` := Y and the address steps down Y + 1 rows (`$C0E7` once, then once per count) to the bottom row, and tile `$0D` is queued there. **For Y = 0 none of the side and corner code runs, so the bottom row's edge and right corner are laid over the top row and its left corner stays the top-left `07`** (RUN: `07 0C 0C 0C 0C 0E`) - why the opening animation's first box is not a real box.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): bottom edge and corner
regions.description: For X non-zero a run of X tiles `$0C` and, at `$18` + X + 1, the corner `$0E`; the caller's address is restored and Y = height comes back in Y. `RTS`.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): choose a tile (`$8C76`)
regions.description: `ROR $1B / ROL $1B` leaves `$1B` unchanged and sets the flags: non-zero returns A (the tile asked for), zero returns `$20`.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): queue one tile (`$8C7F`)
regions.description: Reserve 4 bytes (`JSR $C04B` = `$D6D3`, waiting for room), take the queue offset (`$C03C`) in Y and write `[count 1][$19][$18]`; the caller stores the tile at `$0103,Y` and commits with `JSR $C03F`. Y is clobbered (the height is kept in `$1A`).

regions.name: Table, 23 bytes
regions.description: A table of 23 bytes at $913A, read by LDA aby at $91BA. THE EXTENT COMES FROM THE CODE, not from the data: the same routine reads another table based at $9151 from $91C3, 9 bytes away in the instruction stream, so this table runs exactly up to that base. Two bases read by unrelated code would bound nothing, which is why the reads have to be neighbours. **WHAT THE BYTES MEAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED** - this region claims the extent and the reader and stops there. Generated by tools/find-tables.py.

regions.name: Boss object type, by corridor
regions.description: Bank 3 $91B8: LDY $51 / LDA $913A,Y -> $71, then (skipped for corridor 21 by CPY #$15 / BEQ) LDA $9151,Y ($91C3) -> $72, the type bank 3 $92E5 spawns for the boss phase and $92EE waits on. Values by corridor 0-22: 06 40 45 2E 46 23 47 06 49 18 19 2D 41 4C 25 24 2F 06 48 4D 26 4D 4F. Corridor 1's $40 is CONFIRMED against hardware: the owner's savestate of the corridor 1 boss fight (Fleepa) has $51 = 1, $72 = $40 and slot 23 of type $C0, drawn exactly as type $40's handler draws it (41/41 sprites). Types $40 and $41 share that handler, so corridor 12's $41 is presumably Fleepa again - a lead. The other entries are not tied to names. The 23 is a structural extent (to the next table), and the last entries may never be read; a LEAD on the extent.

regions.name: Table, 23 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $9240, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $917F, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Fill: 40 x $FF
regions.description: 40 bytes of $FF running from the end of the bank's last claimed structure to $BFFE, the byte before the bank-identity byte at $BFFF that the reset path checks. No reader has been found; $FF is the erased-EPROM value, so this reads as unused space.

regions.name: Bank 3 identity byte
regions.description: One byte at $BFFF, the last byte of PRG bank 3, holding the bank's own number. Banks 0 to 6 each carry one; bank 7 does not, because bank 7's last byte is at $FFFF and belongs to the IRQ vector. These seven bytes are the ROM half of a boot-time mapper self-test. $FF23-$FF43, reached from the reset handler, is a loop over Y = 6 down to 0: TYA / JSR $D705 selects the bank in Y, CPY $BFFF then compares Y against the byte this region holds, and BEQ $FF41 falls through to DEY only when the two agree. If they do not, LDA $FF3A,Y fetches a per-bank code, stores it at $0180, calls $DED2 and then spins forever at JMP $FF37. So the game refuses to start unless every one of the seven switchable banks can be selected and answers with its own number - which is the check a UxROM board needs, because a bus conflict on the latch fails silently and leaves the wrong bank mapped. Reading the byte at $BFFF works no matter which bank is live precisely because every bank has one at the same address and they all differ. NOT ESTABLISHED: what $DED2 does with $0180, and therefore whether the failure is displayed or merely hangs.

regions.name: BANK 4 ENTRY: the screen-data block of a corridor (`$8000`)
regions.description: `JMP $8003`: **the single entry**. A = the corridor number (`$FF` and `$FE` are the launch and landing blocks): `$8003` adds 2, doubles it, and returns the block's pointer from the 25-entry table at `$8013` in `$19:$18` - code that returns DATA, which is why the trace saw only these 19 bytes. Called through bank 4 by the corridor loaders of bank 7 (`$EF6C` and the launch / landing code).

regions.name: BANK 4 ENTRY: the pointer lookup (`$8003`)
Per-area screen-data block pointers
regions.description: 25 little-endian pointers, $8013-$8044, each naming a block in this bank. Read by this bank's only entry point: $8000 jumps to $8003, which does CLC / ADC #$02 / ASL A / TAY and then LDA $8013,Y / STA $18 and LDA $8014,Y / STA $19, returning the block address in $18/$19. So entry n sits at $8017 + 2n and the index arrives in A. THE INDEX IS THE AREA NUMBER: bank 7 $EF9B switches to bank 4, $EF9E does LDA $51 and $EFA0 calls $8000. $51 is bounded by CPY #$15 at $F2E2, which is 21 - and 21 areas is what the game has. The table's own 25 entries reach two slots below the index-zero entry and two above index 21, and what those four are for is NOT established. The upper bound on the table is structural: entry 2 points at $8045, the byte immediately after the table, so the table cannot extend past $8044. This is how bank 4 is reached at all - the bank sat at 19 traced bytes of 16,384 because its entry point returns a pointer instead of running code, and nothing static followed the pointer.

regions.name: Fill: 14 x $FF
regions.description: 14 bytes of $FF before the bank-identity byte at $BFFF. No reader.

regions.name: Bank 4 identity byte
regions.description: One byte at $BFFF, the last byte of PRG bank 4, holding the bank's own number. Banks 0 to 6 each carry one; bank 7 does not, because bank 7's last byte is at $FFFF and belongs to the IRQ vector. These seven bytes are the ROM half of a boot-time mapper self-test. $FF23-$FF43, reached from the reset handler, is a loop over Y = 6 down to 0: TYA / JSR $D705 selects the bank in Y, CPY $BFFF then compares Y against the byte this region holds, and BEQ $FF41 falls through to DEY only when the two agree. If they do not, LDA $FF3A,Y fetches a per-bank code, stores it at $0180, calls $DED2 and then spins forever at JMP $FF37. So the game refuses to start unless every one of the seven switchable banks can be selected and answers with its own number - which is the check a UxROM board needs, because a bus conflict on the latch fails silently and leaves the wrong bank mapped. Reading the byte at $BFFF works no matter which bank is live precisely because every bank has one at the same address and they all differ. NOT ESTABLISHED: what $DED2 does with $0180, and therefore whether the failure is displayed or merely hangs.
