Zeroes the speed $B8/$B9, the row hand-off $A5, the row cycle $A1 and the scroll variables ($D4FD), sets the row counter $B0/$B1 = $FFFF, the pixel counter $AF = $0F, the row index $AE = $0D and the half flag $AB = 1, sets $30 bit 4 (the NMI moves the split marker), writes $80 to $0400-$0407 (the overlay slots' state bytes: $80 = free, as the corridor model assumes), reads the first trigger from the block's first two bytes into $B2/$B3, points the record pointer $BC/$BD just after them, sets $B0/$B1 = trigger - 1 (so the first new row brings the counter exactly to the first trigger) and the speed target $BA/$BB = $0200 (2 px a frame).

regions.name: Prime the screen: build one full screen of rows before the scroll starts
regions.description: Loads the attribute patterns ($EE09, $0199-$01A0), waits for the decompressor, then repeats: save the speed, set it to $1000 (16 px a frame, one row per pass), one scroll step ($E530), restore the speed, run the row accounting at $E69B (which builds a row because $AF starts at $0F), wait for queue room ($E5EB); it ends when the row index $AE is back at $0D with the half flag $AB clear, i.e. after a whole cycle of 15 rows (240 pixels). RUN (corridor 5 start, take-off): $E5BD entered at frame 18, the loop body ran 15 times, 15 rows went through the direct-row path ($E619), and the first stage step of the flight came at frame 26.

regions.name: Wait until the PPU queue has room and no row is half-sent
regions.description: Loop: X = queue offset $21. At $31 or more it runs the main-thread flush ($E605) and tries again; below that, no pending row ($A5 = 0) returns; $A5 = 2 (the second tile row of a background row still to go) with offset under $0E takes the direct-row path at $E619 and returns; any other pending value ($A5 = 1 or 3, or 2 with a fuller queue) flushes and tries again. With rendering on the flush does nothing, so the loop is a spin waiting for the NMI to drain (the ~12,600 hits per room exit); with rendering off it drains the queue itself. Callers: $E5DD, $E6B0 and the room-scroll bands ($F001, $F186, $F204).

regions.name: Flush the PPU queue from the main thread (only while the screen is off)
regions.description: If PPUMASK's shadow $FE has bits 3-4 set (rendering on) it returns: the NMI will do it. Otherwise $D7AA turns the NMI off for a moment (waiting for a frame boundary on $2B), $DD54 - the NMI's own queue/row writer - drains the pending row and the queue, and $FF/PPUCTRL are restored with the NMI enabled again.

regions.name: Send the second tile row of a background row straight into the queue
regions.description: Reached from $E5FD when $A5 = 2 and the queue offset is under $0E (the entry then fits below the $31 limit). Saves the pending count $20, clears it and $A5, appends [$20 (32-tile run)][$AD][$AC OR $20] + the 32 tiles of $0150-$016F at the queue offset (offset + 35), and sets the pending count to the saved value + 1. So the row's second half joins the queue instead of waiting for the NMI's own transfer. RUN: 15 hits during the priming loop.

regions.name: Stage step (every frame): end-of-stage test and mode test
regions.description: Called once per frame from the game loop ($FF7A, slot $C14A). $B7 = 0 (no scroll this frame), $A0 bit 2 cleared (the wave-wait flag), $A0 bit 0 (end of stage: a boss beaten or a room exit taken) jumps to $EB18; then BIT $30: bit 6 clear (the labyrinth) skips straight to the loader at $E6A6.

regions.name: Stage step: scroll, then ramp the speed toward the target
regions.description: Entry $E66A (slot $C15C; also called by the flight loops) runs the scroll step $E530, then compares the 16-bit speed $B9:$B8 with the target $BB:$BA: smaller -> +2, larger -> -2, equal -> unchanged (an unsigned compare; the 'at once' bit of a speed command is applied by the command, not here). So the speed moves 2/256 px a frame per frame toward the target.

regions.name: Count pixels: a new row every 16
regions.description: $AF += $B7. Below 16 it goes to $E6A6 (push the bank, JMP $E995: the loader and spawn script). At 16 or more it falls into the new-row path with $AF - 16.

regions.name: A new background row is due: wait, count, address
regions.description: $AF -= 16 (carry is set), waits for queue room ($E5EB), $B0/$B1 += 1 (the stage clock: rows since the corridor began), $EACC derives the row's attribute offset $AA and PPU address $AC/$AD from the row index $AE, and while the half flag $AB is 1 adds 8 to $AD (the $2800 alias; the carry is clear after $EACC).

regions.name: Switch to bank 4 for the event stream
regions.description: Pushes the live bank, selects bank 4 ($D748) and sets Y = 0 (the offset into the record at $BC/$BD).

regions.name: Does the next stream record fire on this row?
regions.description: Compares the row counter $B0/$B1 with the record's trigger $B2/$B3. Equal -> $E6EB. Different -> if Y is not 0 add Y to the record pointer $BC/$BD (this is how a handler that has consumed Y bytes moves on: the handlers JMP back here from $E8A8) and go on to build the row from the tables at $E8AB. Entered with Y = 0 from above, so the pointer does not move on that path.

regions.name: Fire a stream record: fetch the command and dispatch
regions.description: A = command byte at ($BC),Y, Y + 1 -> $16 (the operand offset), then JSR $D6AE: the inline jump table that follows ($E6F3, ten two-byte entries, commands 0-9). The records are described under bank 4 in the screen-data notes.

regions.name: Screen-data command dispatch
regions.description: Ten entries, $E6F3-$E706, each holding a handler address minus one - the inline jump table convention of $D6B0, which pushes the two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back. $E6EB reads a command byte through ($BC), the walking pointer into the bank 4 block, and hands it unmasked to $D6AE, so the command set is exactly $00-$09. THE COUNT IS BOUNDED BY STRUCTURE, not by the code: the tenth entry ends at $E706 and handler 0 begins at $E707, so the table stops exactly where its own first target starts. Reading an eleventh entry gives $16A5, which is RAM. Handlers: $E707, $E721, $E733, $E760, $E78A, $E79F, $E7B6, $E85E, $E881, $E893. All ten are now traced. WHAT EACH ONE DOES is not established.

regions.name: Stream command 0: set the scroll speed target
regions.description: Two operand bytes -> the target $BA/$BB (the high byte's bit 7 is a flag, not part of the value). With bit 7 clear the speed ramps toward it by 2/256 a frame ($E66A). With bit 7 set the value (high byte AND $7F) is also copied into the current speed $B8/$B9 at once. RUN: the flight block and corridors 3 and 15 fire it at frame 18 and 382 of a corridor start (the flight's, then the corridor's own). Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 1: choose the background row table
regions.description: Two operand bytes -> the row table pointer $B4/$B5 ([rows lo][rows hi][count]) and the row cycle $A1 = 0, so the strip starts again from its first row. Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 2: start or stop enemy waves
regions.description: One operand byte: its low two bits replace the low two bits of $60 (bit 1 = a spawn script is running; bit 0 is written with it and tested by nothing). If bit 1 is set two more operand bytes follow: the script pointer -> $66/$67, the wait counters $68 = $69 = 1 and the script bank $7F = 4 - a spawn script that lives in bank 4 and is run by the same interpreter ($F78F) as the labyrinth's, its waits counted in rows (the $A0 bit 2 flag). RUN: fired at frame 19 and 382 in corridors 3 and 15. Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 3: jump to another block (the loop)
regions.description: Two operand bytes = a block address. The block's first two bytes (its first trigger) are copied into BOTH the next-trigger $B2/$B3 and the row counter $B0/$B1, the record pointer $BC/$BD is set to block + 2, and it re-enters the trigger test at $E6CC. So a jump also REBASES THE STAGE CLOCK to the target's first trigger and the target's first record fires on this very row. The launch flight's block ends with it: it fired at frames 186, 236, 287 and 338 of a corridor start (every ~50 frames: the flight's overlay pattern loops). Command 9 enters this code at $E762 when its condition holds.

regions.name: Stream command 4: set the background palettes
regions.description: Two operand bytes = a palette list address -> $18/$19, then JSR $D92D (the palette-list walker: up to eight indices, $FE ends, $FF skips; far-calls bank 5 $B2E4). Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 5: the boss phase
regions.description: Sets $70 = 1 (the boss routine in bank 3 $917F starts the fight). In corridor 21 ($51 = $15) one operand byte follows and becomes the boss type $72; in every other corridor there is no operand (the DEY cancels the Y that the tail adds). The record is therefore one byte longer in corridor 21 only. Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 6: place a structure in an overlay slot
regions.description: Operand 1 = the number of placements (0 = none). Each placement: a flag byte (low three bits = the slot 0-7 -> X; bit 7 no delay and no gap; bit 6 no step byte; bit 5 a single showing; bit 4 the structure is given inline), then in order: [delay -> $0430,X] and [gap -> $0408,X] unless bit 7 (bit 5 set stores $20 as the gap, which is never used because it also means one repeat), [step -> $0438,X] unless bit 6 (else 0), [repeats -> $0410,X] unless bit 5 (else 1; 0 = for ever), the start column -> $0400,X, then either [pointer lo][pointer hi][width][height] inline (bit 4: -> $0440/$0448, $0420, $0418) or a pointer to a structure [width][height][rows] (the pointer + 2 -> $0440/$0448). $EA79 then loads the working pointer $0450/$0458 and the row counter $0428 from them. The table in tools/tgl/corridor.py ('placements') reads the same format and is what the stage pictures use. Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 7: load graphics for the stage
regions.description: While the art-load stream engine is busy ($27 non-zero) it runs a step of it ($E99F) and waits for the decompressor ($D7C3), then loops. Then two operand bytes -> the stream address $28/$29, $27 = $80 (start) and the stream's bank $7E = 4. The records are run by $E995/$E99F one step per row. Used 5 rows before a boss to swap the art (the squares before a boss). Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 8: set attribute patterns
regions.description: Pairs [index < 8][value] -> $0199,index (the attribute patterns the metatile drawer ORs in), repeated while the index byte is below 8. This command does not occur in any block (the parser finds it zero times); it is read from the code only. Every handler ends by jumping to $E89D, which skips its last operand byte, reads the NEXT record's trigger into $B2/$B3 and returns to $E6CE with Y = the bytes consumed.

regions.name: Stream command 9: the jump taken only in the boss phase
regions.description: If $70 is non-zero (a command 5 has run) it enters the jump code at $E762; otherwise it skips its two operand bytes (the INY here and the one in the tail). The corridor blocks use it as the end of a loop: the stage repeats until the boss is called, then falls through into the ending records.

regions.name: Record tail: read the next trigger and go back to the test
regions.description: INY over the last operand byte, the next record's trigger -> $B2/$B3 (low, high), INY, and JMP $E6CE with Y = the bytes this record used. $E6CE then fires the next record on the same row if its trigger is the same, or adds Y to the record pointer and builds the row.

regions.name: Build a row: take the next 16 ids from the strip
regions.description: $A1 (the row cycle) is compared with the row table's count byte; at or over it wraps to 0; it is then incremented. The 16 ids are at (table pointer) + 16 x the old $A1 (computed by shifting left four times into $19), and are copied into $04C0-$04CF: the background row, before any overlay is drawn over it.

regions.name: Build a row: draw the eight overlay slots over it
regions.description: For each slot X = 0-7 ($15): column $0400,X = $80 is a free slot and is skipped. A running delay $0430,X is decremented and the slot skipped. Otherwise one ROW of the structure is drawn: the working pointer $0450/$0458 is read with the codes $00 n (skip n columns: the column counter moves on), $01 (end the row early) and any other value = a metatile id written to $04C0 + column when the column is under 16, until `width` ($0420) ids have been written; the pointer is saved for the next row. When the height $0428 runs out ($0428 counts down once per row): if the repeat counter $0410 is non-zero it is decremented and a result of 0 frees the slot ($0400 = $80); otherwise the column moves by the step $0438, and a column in $20-$EF (off either edge) frees the slot, else $EA73 reloads the gap as the next delay and $EA79 resets the pointer and height - the structure starts again. This is what tools/tgl/corridor.py's simulation does, and it matched a corridor-15 savestate cell for cell (settled rows).

regions.name: Build a row: hand it to bank 5 and step the row index
regions.description: Selects bank 5 and calls its slots $8009 (-> $83B3: draw the 16 metatile ids of $04C0 as tile rows $0130/$0150 and attributes, writing each metatile's fifth byte back) and $802A (-> $89FB: spawn the ground objects named by those fifth bytes), sets $A5 = 1 (a new row is waiting for the NMI) and steps the row index $AE: 14 down to 0 and round again, toggling the half flag $AB at each wrap.

regions.name: Mark that a row came in (the waves' clock)
regions.description: $A0 bit 2 set: the bank 4 spawn script's waits count rows, and this flag is what they see; $E655 clears it again at the next step.

regions.name: Loader and spawn script, then back to the caller's bank
regions.description: Entered by JMP from $E6A9 (no row due) and falling in from $E994 (a row was built) with the caller's bank on the stack: one step of the art-load stream ($E99F), one step of the spawn script interpreter ($F78F), then PLA and JMP $D705 to switch back.

regions.name: Art-load stream: start the next record
regions.description: $27 = 0 means idle (return). Otherwise it selects the stream's bank $7E. A positive $27 is a record already being decompressed (-> $EA21); bit 7 set = start the record at index $27 AND $7F: wait while the decompressor is busy ($0B), read the slot (byte 0 AND $0F), and if that slot ($0480,slot) already holds a block, EVICT it - clear the slot and turn every live object (slots 5-23) that uses the evicted block into type $28, the dissolving square. Then the record: byte 0 = flags | slot, byte 1 = block (0 = none: a 2-byte record that only evicts; bit 7 of byte 0 ends the stream), byte 2 = the first tile; PPU address = tile x 16 -> $18/$19 and the block is armed for decompression ($EA58); $27 counts on.

regions.name: Art-load stream: finish the record
regions.description: Once the decompressor is free ($0B = 0) the record is entered in the slot tables: $0480,slot = the block, $0490,slot = the first tile; $27 moves to the next record, or to 0 (and returns) after a record with bit 7 set. So the tables only change after the tiles are in place.

regions.name: Art-load stream: wait for the decompressor
regions.description: If rendering is on ($FE bits 3-4) it returns and tries again next row; with rendering off it waits for the decompressor ($D7C3) and runs the loader again at once.

regions.name: Arm the decompressor for a block id
regions.description: Block ids under $40 are read from bank 3 (Y = 3); $40 and over from bank 2 with the id reduced by $30 (Y = 2); JMP $D7F9 (slot $C042: arm the decompressor with block A in bank Y).

regions.name: Remove every object but the player
regions.description: Calls the object-removal routine $CCBF (type kept in $0740, the position, velocity and fraction fields zeroed) for slots 1-23. Slot $C159; callers $EB96 and $EBF8 (a room or stage ending) and $F536.

regions.name: Overlay slot: start the gap as the next delay
regions.description: $0430,X := the gap $0408,X, then falls into the reload.

regions.name: Overlay slot: rewind the structure
regions.description: Working pointer $0450/$0458 := the structure's start $0440/$0448, rows left $0428 := the height $0418. Called when a placement is made (from $E854) and when a repeat starts.

regions.name: Allocate an object slot (5-23), reclaiming one if none is free
regions.description: Slot $C027; the spawn-script interpreter calls it. Scans from slot 23 DOWN to 5 for a free one (type 0): returns it in Y with carry clear, so the highest free slot is used first. If none is free it reclaims, in order: the LOWEST slot whose type (AND $7F) is $0B, $0C or $0D; failing that the highest slot with type bit 7 set and flag bit 1 clear in $0578; the reclaimed object is removed ($CCBF) and its slot returned with carry clear. If nothing can be reclaimed it returns carry set (Y = 4). RUN with all slots full of type $10: carry set; a $0B in slot 12 and a $0D in 15 reclaimed 12; bit-7 types in 8 and 14 reclaimed 14; a bit-7 type with flag bit 1 set was left alone; X preserved. What types $0B-$0D are was not looked up.

regions.name: Row address: the background row's PPU address and attribute offset
regions.description: From the row index $AE (0-14): the attribute offset $AA = (AE AND 14) x 4 + $C0 (low byte of the attribute address), and $AC/$AD = the row's PPU address from the pair table at $EAE2 (one entry per 64 bytes, $2000 ... $23C0; the band's second tile row is +$20). The caller adds 8 to $AD for the $2800 alias.

regions.name: Table, 1 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $E462, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to next read base $EAE3, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Table, 29 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $E458, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $EB00, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Table, 4 bytes
regions.description: A table of 4 bytes at $EB00, read by LDA aby at $D8CE. THE EXTENT COMES FROM THE CODE, not from the data: the same routine reads another table based at $EB04 from $D8D4, 6 bytes away in the instruction stream, so this table runs exactly up to that base. Two bases read by unrelated code would bound nothing, which is why the reads have to be neighbours. **WHAT THE BYTES MEAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED** - this region claims the extent and the reader and stops there. Generated by tools/find-tables.py.

regions.name: Table, 4 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $D8D4, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $EB08, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Place the ship at the start position
regions.description: Slot 0's x := $78, y := $90 and its facing $0668 := 4 (down). Called by the game start ($EB37) and after a corridor in a TGL-less game ($ECF0). RUN: (120, 144), facing 4.

regions.name: THE TRANSITION DISPATCHER: new game, or the ship is already playing
regions.description: Entered by JMP from the stage step ($E663) when $A0 bit 0 is set (a room exit or a finished stage), and at the very start of a game. Slot 0's type $0500 = 0 means there is no ship yet: this is the START OF A GAME ($EB1D); anything else is a transition during play ($EB78). This routine does not return until the new room or corridor is up and begun ($ED1D); the loop is suspended meanwhile (see the room-change scrolls).

regions.name: Game start: HUD labels and the move history
regions.description: $E15F draws the HUD labels. If the start mode $2F is below 3 (0 new game, 1 password, 2 CONTINUE) the ten-byte move history $04F0-$04F9 is filled with 4 ('no move yet'); mode 3 (the progress recorder) keeps it. RUN: modes 0 and 2 gave all 4, mode 3 kept $77.

regions.name: Game start: reset the mode, ship, and find the room
regions.description: $2F := 0, bank 5, the ship placed ($EB08), exit code $A4 := 4, bank 5 $802D (-> $8071: applies the exit $A4 to the position ($52, $53) - 4 means no move - and builds the neighbour record pointers $E0-$E8, $E4 being the room itself). Then $30 bit 5 (a labyrinth special-screen game: CONTINUE or a password restores one) goes to $EB60, otherwise the corridor start below.

regions.name: Game start: corridor 0 (or a random corridor in the demo)
regions.description: $50 := 0, $51 := 0 (corridor 0, the opening stage), $77 := 0 (the TGL order index). In a demo ($30 bit 7) $51 := a random value AND $0F (corridors 0-15). $D4F3 switches the NMI on and it jumps to the corridor loader $EC94. RUN: $51 = 0 in a normal start, 5 in a demo run (random).

regions.name: Game start with a saved labyrinth position (CONTINUE / password)
regions.description: A TGL game has no labyrinth and goes to the corridor start ($EB5A). Otherwise it loads the labyrinth ship's sprite sheet and the weapon sprites ($F6F5, $F717) and looks at the map record at $E4 (the player's position): byte 0 bit 7 (a special screen) -> $EC23, an ordinary room -> $EC76. RUN, CONTINUE with $2F = 2: place ship, 802D, F6F5, F717, EEE0 ... fade in, begin play at frame 83; TGL: the corridor loader at once.

regions.name: A transition during play: the move history
regions.description: $A4 is the exit that was taken (0 N, 2 W, 6 E, 8 S, 4 = into a corridor). Unless it is 4 the ten-byte history $04F0-$04F9 is shifted up one place and $A4 stored at $04F0 (the newest). The history feeds the seal puzzle (seven alternating moves) and the loop gates. RUN: exit 0 gave [0, 4, 4 ...], exit 6 [6, 4, 4 ...].

regions.name: Which kind of exit? ($A0 bit 1)
regions.description: $A0 bit 1 set goes to the warp-style exit at $EBD4; clear is an ordinary room change. The bit is set (with bit 0) by two places found by scanning for ORA #$03 / STA $A0: bank 3 $9009 (the ship on a warp panel with the right key, sound $3B) and bank 1 $8057 (the gate's ship being pushed up). CORRECTION: ram.json called it 'the player died'; the death goes through bank 6 $8239 to GAME OVER instead.

regions.name: Transition: forget the open box, clear the objects, corridor or labyrinth?
regions.description: $56 := $FF (no pick-up box is open), every object but the ship removed ($EA68), bank 5. $30 bit 6 clear (the labyrinth) -> $EBA5. In a corridor: not a demo -> the stage end at $EBFE; in a demo JMP $FF4A (the demo is over, the game restarts).

regions.name: Room change: after a miniboss, restore the room music
regions.description: If the boss phase $70 is set (a miniboss was just beaten) it plays sound $1F and then the labyrinth music of the area, $EF16[$50] (the area table), and clears $70.

regions.name: Room change: load the next room and begin
regions.description: The order, RUN: bank 5 $802D (moves the position $52/$53 one cell in the direction $A4 and rebuilds the neighbour pointers $E0-$E8; CORRECTION: an earlier note gave this to $8015), $8015 (read the record at $E4), $8003 (build the room buffer), $8030, $F09A (the scroll, which ends by calling $8006 for the cell classes), $ED44 (the key-door pictures), $8039, then A = 0 and JMP $ED1D (begin play, no jingle). RUN: the north exit took 81 frames in all, the east exit 98; ($52, $53) went (8, 12) -> (8, 11) and (9, 12).

regions.name: Warp-style exit: flash the ship
regions.description: If the exit is not 4 (into a corridor) slot 0's $0578 is set to bit 7 on, bit 6 off, its $0788 := $80 and 60 game-loop passes run ($FF8B, Y = $3C): the ship's leaving animation. Exit code 4 skips it. RUN: 59 frames to $EBEE.

regions.name: Warp-style exit: remove the ship and the objects
regions.description: Slot 0 := type 0, 20 more passes, every object removed, bank 5. RUN: $EBFE at frame 79 (60 + 20); with exit code 4 at frame 19.

regions.name: Where to? Read the target record
regions.description: $70 := 0; X = $A4; $18/$19 := the map record of the neighbour in that direction (the pointer table at $E0: N $E0, W $E2, own room $E4, E $E6, S $E8). If $30 has bit 5 or 6 set (a special screen or a corridor) it goes to $EC54, otherwise to the next block.

regions.name: Go to a SPECIAL SCREEN (fade, sound, load)
regions.description: $EDD1 fade out, sound $1F, $D4E3 (NMI off), $F269 (not read), bank 5 $802D. RUN: the fade took 8 frames, sound $1F at frame 87, EE1D at 87.

regions.name: Special screen: draw it and the key-door pictures
regions.description: JSR $EE1D (loads the screen type $51 and its scene, see the labyrinth notes) and $ED44. Also reached by JMP from $EB75 and $ECF3.

regions.name: Special screen: clear the ship, set sprite 0
regions.description: Slot 0 := type 0, $36 := 0, sprite 0's y $BF ($D51E), then a far call to bank 6 $8000 (one object-loop pass; the three inline bytes at $EC38).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $EC38
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $EC35 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 6 $8000**. The stored word is $7FFF rather than $8000 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Special screen: fade in, and the gate-cleared ship entrance
regions.description: Scroll zeroed ($D4FD), fade in ($ED98). Screen type $51 = 5 (a corridor gate whose corridor is cleared) goes to $EC4C; anything else begins play with A = $80, i.e. WITH the jingle ($ED1D).

regions.name: Cleared gate: the scripted ship entrance
regions.description: JSR $F4B7 (the type-$81 ship entrance, see the stage-clear notes), then begin play with A = 0 (no jingle).

regions.name: Special screen or corridor?
regions.description: $30 AND $60 = $20 (a labyrinth special screen) -> $EC5B; otherwise (bit 6: a corridor) JMP $ECBD, the stage end.

regions.name: Leaving a special screen: into a corridor, another special screen, or a room
regions.description: Exit code 4 (the gate) -> $EC8C. Otherwise the neighbour's record: byte 0 bit 7 set (another special screen) -> $EC12, else an ordinary room -> $EC65. RUN: exit W with a special record went through EC12 and EE1D, with an ordinary one through EC65 and EEE0.

regions.name: Leaving to an ordinary room: fade, load, fade in
regions.description: $EDD1 fade out, sound $1F, NMI off, $F269, bank 5 $802D, $EEE0 (read the area, load the scene, build and draw the room), $ED44, scroll zeroed, sprite 0, $ED98 fade in, begin play with A = $80 (the jingle). RUN: $EEE0 at frame 87, begin play at 110 with sound $3C.

regions.name: Into a corridor from its gate
regions.description: The corridor number = byte 2 of the gate's map record ($18),2 AND $7F -> $51. RUN: the record of corridor 5's entrance ($8C09) gave $51 = 5 after 19 frames (the 20-pass wait of $EBEE).

regions.name: CORRIDOR LOAD: start corridor $51
regions.description: Entered from the gate, the game start, and the end of each corridor. Sound $1F (the pre-corridor jingle), the corridor launch $F282 (fade, the take-off flight), $EF6C (the corridor's scene and stream), the ship at (128, 160) ($0530/$0518), sprite 0, the fade in ($ED98), the corridor's music $EF2A[$51], then begin play with A = 0. Bank 5 must be live on entry (the launch calls bank 5 $8000).

regions.name: STAGE END: which corridor was it?
regions.description: Reached by JMP from $EC58. $51 = 0 -> $ECE7; 1-20 -> $ECE4 (mark it cleared first); 21 -> $ECC7; 22 -> $ECE1.

regions.name: Corridor 21: the clear, then the planet cutscene
regions.description: $F506 (stage clear), then a far call to bank 0 $8012 (the starfield, $88F5; inline bytes at $ECCD).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $ECCD
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $ECCA - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 0 $8012**. The stored word is $8011 rather than $8012 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Corridor 21: reload the ship's sprites
regions.description: $F6E5 and $F717.

regions.name: Corridor 21: the planet scene
regions.description: Far call to bank 2 $801B ($8836: the planet scene; the three inline bytes at $ECD9).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $ECD9
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $ECD6 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 2 $801B**. The stored word is $801A rather than $801B because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Corridor 21: on to corridor 22
regions.description: $51 += 1 (22) and JMP $EC94: the last corridor loads. See the ending notes.

regions.name: Corridor 22: the clear (never returns)
regions.description: $F506 runs the final score screen and the ending; it does not return.

regions.name: Corridors 1-20: mark cleared
regions.description: $EFBA marks the corridor cleared (the flags the map reads, $04A9/$04AA; read, not run).

regions.name: Corridors 0-20: the clear; then labyrinth or TGL?
regions.description: $F506 (stage clear, key, the landing flight), then $30 bit 1 set (a TGL game) goes to $ECF6, otherwise back to the labyrinth.

regions.name: Back to the labyrinth
regions.description: The ship placed ($EB08) and the special screen / room at the player's position drawn ($EC23).

regions.name: TGL: the item screen
regions.description: Far call to bank 3 $8018 (YOU GOT ITEM, the reward screen; inline bytes at $ECF9).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $ECF9
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $ECF6 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 3 $8018**. The stored word is $8017 rather than $8018 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: TGL: the next corridor
TGL game: corridor order
regions.description: $ECFC: LDY $77 / INC $77 / LDA $ED08,Y / STA $51 / JMP $EC94 - the next corridor, reached only when $30 bit 1 is set (the TGL password's corridors-only game) after the reward screen. $77 starts at 0 ($EB18). 1, 11, 12, 2, 13, 3, 14, 4, 15, 5, 16, 6, 17, 7, 18, 8, 19, 9, 20, 10, 21: every corridor 1-21 exactly once, which is the check on the 21 entries; after 21 $ECBD takes the ending path instead of reading a 22nd.

regions.name: Begin play: the entry jingle
regions.description: Entered by JMP from the room and corridor loaders ($EBD1, $EC49, $EC51, $EC89, $ECBB). A = 0 or $80 is the caller's flag: it is stored in slot 0's $0578 and its bit 7 tested at once. With bit 7 set in the labyrinth ($30 bit 6 clear) sound $3C plays (the room-entry jingle; id not looked up); in a corridor, or with A = 0, nothing. RUN: A = $80 in the labyrinth played $3C; A = 0 and A = $80 in a corridor played nothing. The $0578 value stays in the slot until the ship's handler re-initialises it (not checked).

regions.name: Begin play: make the ship, clear the end-of-stage flags
regions.description: Slot 0 := type 1 (the player's ship) with $0788 := $40 (its phase counter; not looked up), $A0 bits 0-1 cleared (end of stage / the player died), $E15F redraws the HUD labels and the AREA/X/Y row, and JMP $D762 selects bank 6 (the object loop's bank) and returns. RUN: $0500 = 1, $0788 = $40, $A0 AND 3 = 0, bank 6 live afterwards.

regions.name: Key doors: arm each exit's hit counter
regions.description: Called when a room loads ($EBC9, $EC26, $EC79). ORs $30 into the four exit bytes $58-$5B (N, W, E, S): the high nibble becomes 3, the number of shots a key-door cover still takes, the low nibble is the key the exit needs (8 = open, no door). RUN: (3, 8, 8, 5) became $33 $38 $38 $35.

regions.name: Key doors: the first key's picture
regions.description: $19:$18 = PPU $1000. Scans the four exits for the first whose key (low nibble) is not 8; if there is none it returns. Otherwise it keeps that key and far-calls bank 2 slot $8006 (-> $8212, the key-icon builder; the 3 inline bytes follow) with A = the key, building its icon in background tiles $00-$03. RUN: exits (3, 8, 8, 5): the builder was called with A = 3 at $1000.

regions.name: Far-call argument at $ED6E
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $ED6B - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 2 $8006**. The stored word is $8005 rather than $8006 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Key doors: a second key's picture
regions.description: $19:$18 = PPU $1040. Scans the exits again for the first whose key is neither 8 nor the one just built; if found, far-calls the icon builder with that key (tiles $04-$07). RUN: (3, 8, 8, 5) built key 5 at $1040; (3, 3, 8, 8), (1, 8, 8, 1) and (8, 8, 2, 8) built one icon only; (4, 5, 3, 8) built 4 at $1000 and 5 at $1040 (the third key, 3, gets no picture: at most two keys are drawn per room). CHR: with keys 3 and 5 the tiles at $1000 equalled the icon built for key 3 alone, and at $1040 the icon for key 5 alone. The live CHR of the labyrinth savestate room, which has no key door, holds a generic picture there whose high plane equals the key icons' (they share one high plane), so the ring and bracket the cell notes mention are, as an inference not checked on screen, these tiles: the generic picture when no door needs a key, the key's own picture when one does.

regions.name: Far-call argument at $ED8E
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $ED8B - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 2 $8006**. The stored word is $8005 rather than $8006 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Key doors: return
regions.description: The RTS the far call comes back to.

regions.name: Key doors: next exit
regions.description: INY, and the scan loop of the second pass continues until all four exits are done.

regions.name: Fade IN: the screen comes up from black
regions.description: Callers $EC3E, $EC84, $ECAE (after a room or corridor is drawn with the screen off). $EDA1 turns the live palette into the target and blanks the screen colours, $EDE8 switches the display back on, then JMP $EDBD fades. RUN: from black the 24 palette bytes stepped $0F -> $00-hue -> +$10 per step to their saved values in 5 steps, 8 frames, ending with the palette restored, $A3 = $18 (rendering on) and the NMI enabled.

regions.name: Fade set-up: save the palette, black the screen
regions.description: Copies the 24 live palette bytes $0181-$0198 to the fade target $04D0-$04E7 and sets each live byte to $0F (black); $017F = 3 asks the NMI to upload both the background and the sprite palettes. The backdrop $0180 is not touched.

regions.name: Fade IN, entry 2
regions.description: Slot $C0DE. The same set-up, then a wait for the start of vblank ($EDF4) and into the fade loop. The display is NOT switched on by this entry (the caller does that).

regions.name: Fade loop
regions.description: $D950 steps every palette byte one notch toward its target: a byte already equal is left; a byte at $0F jumps to the target's hue at its darkest ($0X); otherwise the brightness (high nibble) goes up $10 if the hue matches and the byte is below the target, and down $10 in every other case (so a different hue fades out first), a borrow giving $0F. $15 counts the bytes that moved and $017F = 3 asks for the upload. When nothing moved the loop returns. With the NMI enabled ($FF bit 7) it waits 2 frames between steps ($FFD1); with the NMI off it does all the steps at once with no waiting. So a colour at brightness 3 takes four steps to black and a fade lasts 8 frames.

regions.name: Fade OUT: the screen goes to black and is switched off
regions.description: Slot $C0ED; many callers ($EC12, $EC65, $F282, $F439, $F65E, $F66B, $F6B8, $FF65). Sets the 24 target bytes $04D0-$04E7 and the backdrop $0180 to $0F, runs the fade loop, then SEI and JMP $D4C7 (rendering off: $A3 = 0 and the PPUMASK bits cleared). RUN: 5 steps at frames 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 ($30 -> $20 -> $10 -> $00 -> $0F for the first colour), returned at frame 8 with all colours $0F, $A3 = 0 and the I flag set.

regions.name: Screen on: sprite 0, the DMC timer, rendering
regions.description: $EDE5 (slot $C060) first sets sprite 0's y from A ($D51E); $EDE8 stores $87 in $05 and in the DMC rate register $4010 (the split timer's starting rate: see the DMC entry), calls $EDF4 and enables interrupts (CLI).

regions.name: Wait for vblank, NMI on, two frames, rendering on
regions.description: Slot $C063. Spins on $2002 until the vblank flag has cleared and then set again (the start of a vblank), then $D4F3 (NMI enable), two frames' wait ($FFD1) and JMP $D4D5 (rendering on: $A3 = $18).

regions.name: Load the attribute patterns
regions.description: Copies the 8 bytes at $EE15 (00 55 AA FF 00 55 AA FF: the whole attribute byte for palette 0, 1, 2, 3, twice) to $0199-$01A0, where the metatile drawer indexes them with the fifth metatile byte AND 7. Called by the corridor priming ($E5BD) and the room loader ($EED0).

regions.name: Table, 8 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $EE0B, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $EE1D, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: LOAD A SPECIAL SCREEN: read the record, gate or not?
regions.description: Called by JSR from $EC23. $EECC reads the map record at $E4 and returns its byte 2 in A. Bit 7 set = a CORRIDOR GATE (byte 2 AND $7F is the corridor), clear = another kind of special screen ($EE56). The screen type, 0-8, ends up in $51 (in the labyrinth $51 is the screen type) and the scene is $10 + the type. RUN: $EE1D called from the labyrinth savestate with the position set through bank 5 $802D (with $A4 = 4) on every kind of special record.

regions.name: Gate: the corridor's reward item
regions.description: $55 := $EF40[corridor] (the item the cleared gate holds) and $15 := the corridor number.

regions.name: Gate: has the corridor been cleared?
regions.description: JSR $EFAC tests bit (corridor - 1) of the cleared flags $04A9/$04AA: carry CLEAR = cleared, SET = not cleared. Not cleared goes to $EE3C.

regions.name: Gate, cleared: type 4 or 5
regions.description: $30 bit 6 set -> screen type 5, clear -> type 4. Bit 6 is still set from the corridor just played, so type 5 is the gate seen on RETURNING from the corridor (the ship's scripted entrance $F4B7 follows, and one door cell is opened); type 4 is the same gate on every later visit. RUN: $EE1D called from the labyrinth savestate with the position set through bank 5 $802D (with $A4 = 4) on every kind of special record. Corridor 5 cleared: bit 6 set gave type 5, bit 6 clear gave type 4.

regions.name: Gate, not cleared: sealed gate (8), or corridor 21's special rule
regions.description: Corridors 1-20: type 8, the SEALED GATE (two type-$35 halves, see the seal notes). Corridor 21 ($15 = $15): ($04AA OR $FC) AND $04A9 = $FF means corridors 1-10 are all cleared -> type 8, otherwise type 0 (the gate is shut, no seal puzzle). A cleared corridor 21 takes the cleared path above (type 4 / 5). RUN: nothing cleared 0; 1-9 cleared 0; 1-10 cleared 8; 1-10 and 21 cleared 4.

regions.name: Not a gate: the screen kind from byte 2's low nibble
regions.description: Nibble 1 (the progress recorder) and 3 (a message) keep their number. Nibble 2 and 6 are the round creature's shops: the sub-id $5E is tested in the item flags ($EFE0: the $04A0 array); flag clear keeps 2 / 6, flag SET (already bought) gives 7, the shop after buying. RUN: nibble 2 and 6 gave 2 / 6, and 7 with the flags set; 1 and 3 unchanged.

regions.name: Special screen: scene, area 0, flags
regions.description: $51 := the type, $5C := $10 + the type (the scene number), bank 5 $8000 loads the scene (tile list, metatile sets, palettes), $50 := 0, $30 := ($30 AND $8F) OR $20: the special-screen flag set, the corridor/boss bits cleared. RUN: $30 = $20 afterwards.

regions.name: Special screen: build the room buffer
regions.description: Bank 5 $8003 (-> $8155) builds the 16 x 12 buffer from the type's structure, door set and item list.

regions.name: Special screen type 5: open the gate
regions.description: Only for type 5: the four buffer cells $0740 + $37, + $72, + $7D, + $A7 that hold metatile 8 (the door) become metatile $0C (open), through $EEB7. RUN: in corridor 5's gate the cell at +$72 went 8 -> 12 for type 5 and stayed 8 for types 4 and 8 (the other three cells held other metatiles in this gate's layout).

regions.name: Special screen: classes, draw, and the screen's objects
regions.description: Bank 5 $8006 (the cell classes), $EFF3 with A = $20 (draw the whole room into nametable 0, spawning the ground objects), bank 5 $8036 (-> $A430: the screen's own set-up; not read).

regions.name: Special screen: slot 5 and the screen's sound
regions.description: $0505 (slot 5's type) := $35, the gate halves' type, for every special screen (the screens that have no gate presumably overwrite or ignore it; not checked); then A = $EF21[type] and, if not 0, JMP $D852 plays it. The table is indexed by the SCREEN TYPE 0-8: $10 $18 $18 $13 $10 0 $18 $18 $12. RUN: sounds $10 (type 0), $18 (1, 2, 6, 7), $13 (3), $10 (4), none (5), $12 (8). CORRECTION: tbl_EF21 was labelled 'corridor sound, first 9 corridors' (a lead) from the misreading that $51 is a corridor here.

regions.name: Open one door cell
regions.description: In: X = an offset into the room buffer $0740. If the cell holds metatile 8 it becomes $0C.

regions.name: Palette-list-shaped table, no reader found
regions.description: 00 01 02 03 05 06 09 0A: eight values, all below 36, which is the shape of a list for the palette walker at $D92D (see bank0.pal_82BD). LEAD: nothing reads it. No absolute or indexed operand names $EEC1-$EECC, no LDA #$C4 / LDA #$EE pair builds the pointer, and no 16-bit word $EEC4 exists anywhere in the ROM. It sits right after an RTS ($EEC3) and before the routine at $EECC (it reads byte 2 of the room record, $E4).

regions.name: Common start of every room load: read the record
regions.description: $56 := $FF (no pick-up box open), $EE09 loads the attribute patterns, bank 5 $8015 reads the map record at $E4 (set by $802D), bank 5 $8000 with A = 0 loads the common scene 0, and A := the record's byte 2 (Y = 2). Called by the special-screen loader, the ordinary-room loader and the corridor loader ($EF6C).

regions.name: LOAD AN ORDINARY ROOM: byte 2 gives the area
regions.description: Called by JSR from $EC76 and the room paths. A = byte 2 of the record: its HIGH nibble -> $51 (what it means for an ordinary room was not worked out), its LOW nibble -> $50, the labyrinth AREA 0-10; the scene is $5C = area + 5 (so area n is scene n + 5, after the common scenes 0 and 32). RUN: area 0 -> scene 5.

regions.name: Ordinary room: scene, buffer, classes
regions.description: Bank 5 $8000 loads the scene; $30 AND $8F (the special-screen, corridor and boss bits off); $8003 builds the room buffer, $8030 (-> $A3BB: the layout's items and gates: not read through here) and $8006 the cell classes.

regions.name: Ordinary room: draw, and set up the screen's objects
regions.description: $EFF3 with A = $20 draws the room into nametable 0 and spawns its ground objects; bank 5 $8039 (-> $A462: the room's enemy set-up; not read through here).

regions.name: Ordinary room: the area's music
regions.description: A := $EF16[$50] (the labyrinth music by area: 09 07 07 02 02 07 0D 07 02 0D 0E) and JMP $D852 plays it. RUN: area 0 played sound 9.

regions.name: Labyrinth music, by area
regions.description: LDA $EF16,Y with Y = $50, the labyrinth area (bank 7 $EBB0, $EF10 and $FFDE), then JSR/JMP $D852 - the play-sound call - so one song per labyrinth area 0-10. 11 entries, ending where the next table's reads begin at $EF21. Values 09 07 07 02 02 07 0D 07 02 0D 0E.

regions.name: Special-screen sound, by screen type 0-8
regions.description: LDA $EF21,Y with Y = $51 at $EEAF, and in the special-screen loader $51 is the SCREEN TYPE 0-8 (nine values, so the nine bytes are exact), not a corridor. Zero = no sound, otherwise JMP $D852: $10 $18 $18 $13 $10 0 $18 $18 $12. RUN: every type played exactly its entry. CORRECTION: this was named 'Corridor sound, first 9 corridors' and left a lead on the misreading that $51 was a corridor number.

regions.name: Corridor music, by corridor
regions.description: LDA $EF2A,Y with Y = $51 then JSR $D852 at $ECB3. 22 entries, corridors 0-21, ending where $EF40 begins. The values repeat in pairs and then repeat 1-10 for 11-20 - corridors 1-2 share a song, 3-4 another, and corridor n+10 plays what corridor n does - the same pairing the scenes ($EF55) and keys follow.

regions.name: Corridor reward item, by corridor
regions.description: $EE1D: JSR $EECC, and when the result has bit 7 set, AND #$7F / TAY / LDA $EF40,Y / STA $55. 21 entries, ending where $EF55 begins. $EE1D reaches this for a corridor-entrance record; once that corridor is cleared the entrance is screen 5, whose controller $9F75 sets out a type-$31 item in slot 5 - so $55 is the corridor's reward item, an icon number (corridor 0's 25 is never used: there is no entrance 0). CORRECTION to 'what $55 selects is NOT established'. Whether the reward can be taken more than once is not established.

regions.name: Corridor scene, by corridor
regions.description: $EF74: LDY $51 / $EF76 LDA $EF55,Y / STA $5C / JSR bank 5 $8000 - the scene (tiles, metatile sets, palettes, see tools/tgl/scene.py) each corridor loads after scene 1. 23 entries, corridors 0-22, ending exactly where the code at $EF6C begins. CORRECTION: this said 22 and left $EF6B unclaimed; corridor 22, the final one (reached by INC $51 at $ECDC after corridor 21's scene), reads it - scene 32, as corridor 0 does. Values 32 for corridor 0, then pairs 33-38; 11-20 repeat 1-10. HARDWARE: a savestate in corridor 15 has $5C = $23 = $EF55[15].

regions.name: CORRIDOR DATA LOADER: the corridor's scenes
regions.description: Called by JSR from $EC9C, after the launch flight ($F282). $EECC (the common start: $56 := $FF, attribute patterns, read the record at $E4, common scene 0), then bank 5 $8000 with A = 1 (scene 1, the corridors' common scene), then the corridor's own scene $EF55[$51] (23 entries: $20 $21 $21 $22 $22 $23 $23 $24 $24 $26 $26 $21 $21 $22 $22 $23 $23 $24 $24 $25 $25 $25 $20), a wait for the decompressor ($D7C3), and bank 5 $8036 (-> $A430, not read through). RUN (corridor 5, after the flight): $5C = $23 = $EF55[5]; $EF6C at frame 373 of the start, $E560 nine frames later, finished at 390.

regions.name: Corridor start: remember the score
regions.description: Copies the six score bytes $0170-$0175 to $04B9-$04BE (Y = 6 down to 1). The corridor's boss routine turns the difference into the points gained, which the TGL reward uses. RUN with a score of 1..6: $04B9-$04BE = 1..6, $04B8 and $04BF untouched.

regions.name: Corridor start: remember the maximum life
regions.description: $78 := $47. A TGL CONTINUE restores $47 from $78 (see the start-mode notes). RUN.

regions.name: Corridor start: set the corridor flags
regions.description: $30 := ($30 AND $9F) OR $50: bits 6 and 4 set (a corridor; the NMI moves the split marker), bit 5 cleared (not a special screen), bit 7 and the low bits kept. RUN: $A7 -> $D7; after a real start $50.

regions.name: Corridor start: the screen-data block
regions.description: Selects bank 4 and calls its entry $8000 with A = $51, which returns the corridor's block address in $18/$19 (the entry returns a pointer rather than running code).

regions.name: Corridor start: start the stage engine and fill the screen
regions.description: $E560 (reset the row engine, read the block's first trigger) and $E5BD (prime a whole screen of 15 rows at 16 px a frame); see the stage-engine notes. RUN: $E560 at frame 382, the priming finished at 390.

regions.name: Corridor start: back to bank 5
regions.description: JMP $D755: bank 5 is selected and the routine returns to the corridor loader.

regions.name: Is flag (A - 1) set? - the corridor-cleared test
regions.description: In: A = the corridor number c (1-21). Tests bit (c - 1) of the array $04A9-$04AB (corridors 1-8 in $04A9, 9-16 in $04AA, 17-21 in $04AB) through the bit-address helper $EFC7. Out: carry CLEAR = the bit is set (the corridor is cleared), carry SET = not. $EFB5 is shared with the item-flag test below. RUN: after marking 1, 5, 8, 9, 10, 17 and 21 exactly those gave carry clear; the bytes were $91 $03 $11.

regions.name: Mark corridor A cleared
regions.description: Sets bit (A - 1) of $04A9-$04AB. Called from the stage end ($ECE4) for corridors 1-20; the flags are part of the password payload (bytes 0-16 land at $04A0-$04B0). RUN.

regions.name: Bit address: byte index and mask for a bit number
regions.description: Slot $C078. In: A = a bit number n. Out: Y = n / 8, A and $10 = 1 << (n AND 7) (the mask from the 8-byte table at $EFD8). Used by the cleared flags, the item flags and the corridor seals ($04B1/$04B2). RUN: n = 0, 1, 7, 8, 15, 16, 20, 39 gave (Y, mask) = (0,1) (0,2) (0,$80) (1,1) (1,$80) (2,1) (2,$10) (4,$80).

regions.name: Bit masks $01-$80
regions.description: $EFC7 (C078) reads $EFD8,(A AND 7) for a mask and returns A >> 3 in Y as a byte index: the flag-array accessor behind $04B0 (keys), $04A9 (areas) and $04AC (weapon levels).

regions.name: Is item flag A set?
regions.description: Tests bit A of the array at $04A0 (the pick-up and shop flags: a room's sub-id is its flag number). Out: carry CLEAR = set, SET = not, through the shared tail $EFB5. Used by the special-screen loader for the shops and by the item rooms. RUN: flags 0, 9 and 20 set were the only carry-clear results among 0-21.

regions.name: Set item flag A
regions.description: Sets bit A of the array at $04A0. RUN: flags 0, 9, 20 -> $04A0 = $01, $04A1 = $02, $04A2 = $10.

regions.name: Draw a whole room: set up
regions.description: In: A = the high byte of the nametable to draw into ($20 = nametable 0, $24 = nametable 1). Callers: the room load ($EF08), $EEA2 and the room-change scrolls ($F0B1, $F1C8, $F1DC). Band index $AE = 0, room-buffer offset $16 = 0, $17 = A, the scroll step $B7 = 0 and the pixel counter $AF = $20 (advanced 16 a band; nothing here reads it).

regions.name: Draw a whole room: thirteen bands
regions.description: Thirteen times: wait for queue room ($E5EB), draw one band ($F03D), and, when drawing into nametable 0 only ($17 = $20), call bank 5 $802A (-> $89FB: spawn the ground objects the band's metatiles name, through their fifth byte's high nibble). So a room's objects appear once, from the nametable-0 draw; the nametable-1 draw that precedes a scroll spawns nothing. Bands 0-11 are the room's twelve 16-pixel rows (192 bytes of the room buffer $0740, 16 a band); band 12 is the blank row 24. RUN: 13 calls with ($AE, $16) = (0, 0), (1, 16) ... (12, 192). The room buffer must be fresh: it shares its page with the object fields, so after play it is garbage (a redraw of the stale buffer put the wrong tiles in all 192 cells; after bank 5 $8003 rebuilt it, 191 of 192 cells matched the savestate, the odd one being under an object).

regions.name: Draw a whole room: nametable 0 clears the rest
regions.description: Only for nametable 0 ($17 = $20) the three blank fills below run; others jump to the wait at $F03A.

regions.name: Blank row 25 of nametable 0
regions.description: JSR $D5CC (the fill routine); its four inline bytes follow.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 32 blanks at PPU $2320
regions.description: [count $20][$23][$20][value $20]: nametable 0 row 25.

regions.name: Blank rows 26-27 of nametable 0
regions.description: The next fill call.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 64 blanks at PPU $2340
Blank rows 28-29 of nametable 0
regions.description: The third fill call.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 64 blanks at PPU $2380
regions.description: [count $40][$23][$80][value $20]: rows 28 and 29. With band 12 (row 24) the whole of nametable 0 below the room is blank. RUN: after a draw rows 25-29 were all $20.

regions.name: Draw a whole room: wait for the queue to drain
regions.description: JMP $D7C3 (wait for the decompressor and queue); its RTS returns to the caller.

regions.name: Draw one row band: its address
regions.description: Slot-less helper (callers: $F004, the north/south scroll bands $F189 and $F207). $EACC turns the band index $AE into the attribute offset $AA and the PPU address $AC/$AD (the pair table at $EAE2); $AD is ORed with $17, which selects the nametable ($20, $24, or $28 for the corridor-style alias the north scroll uses).

regions.name: Draw one row band: ordinary band or the blank row?
regions.description: $16 is the room-buffer offset of the band: $C0 (192, one past the twelve bands) means the blank row, anything else is an ordinary band.

regions.name: Draw one row band: the blank row 24
regions.description: The row under the room, where the HUD split happens. $10 = 0 for an even band index, $0F for an odd one; the 32 tiles at $0130 are set to $20 (blank) and then tile 0 to $FE, the SOLID SPLIT MARKER (column 0 is what the sprite-0 hit sees); the eight attribute bytes $04E8-$04EF are ANDed with $10 (cleared for an even index, the low nibble kept for an odd one) and the 16 metatile ids $04C0-$04CF zeroed; $A5 = 3 (attributes and one row). RUN: row 24 read FE 20 20 20 ... after a draw.

regions.name: Draw one row band: copy the band's 16 ids
regions.description: 16 bytes from the room buffer $0740 + $16 into $04C0-$04CF (the ids the metatile drawer reads), Y advancing.

regions.name: Draw one row band: draw it and hand it to the NMI
regions.description: $16 = Y (the next band's offset); bank 5 $8009 (-> $83B3) draws the 16 metatiles into the tile rows $0130/$0150 and the attributes $04E8, writing each metatile's fifth byte back; $A5 = 1 (a row is waiting: the NMI sends the attributes and the first tile row, and the second goes into the queue through $E619). Returns. RUN: for the savestate's room the nametable and ALL 64 attribute bytes came out equal to the live ones.

regions.name: Room change: pick the scroll by the exit code
regions.description: Called once, by JSR $EBC6 in the room-change routine, after the new room's data is ready. $A4 is the exit that was taken (set by bank 3 $9045: 0 north, 2 west, 6 east, 8 south): 0 jumps to the north arm $F169, 8 to the south arm $F10D, anything else falls into the horizontal arm at $F0A8. Every arm ends by running the shared tail and a final JMP $8006 (bank 5 $8354, which builds the new room's cell classes), so the whole transition returns to the caller from there. RUN on the labyrinth savestate: the north, south and east exits reached $F169, $F10D and the horizontal arm; west was not run (that room's west side is a wall).

regions.name: East/west scroll: thin the split tile
regions.description: The call to the fill routine $D5CC; the four inline bytes after it are the next region. Tile $FE is the solid split marker: plane 0 all $00, plane 1 all $FF. This clears plane-1 rows 2-7 ($1FEA-$1FEF), leaving only its first two scan lines opaque (measured: 00x8, ff ff 00 00 00 00 00 00). WHY is a LEAD: it is done for the whole horizontal scroll and, for the vertical ones, only after the scroll, for the re-home; the matching restore is the fill at $F1F6.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 6 bytes of $00 at PPU $1FEA
regions.description: [count 6][PPU $1F][$EA][value $00]: $D5CC writes `count` bytes of the value at the address, count 6 here (checked: six CHR bytes changed). Tile $FE is the solid split marker: plane 0 all $00, plane 1 all $FF. This clears plane-1 rows 2-7 ($1FEA-$1FEF), leaving only its first two scan lines opaque (measured: 00x8, ff ff 00 00 00 00 00 00). WHY is a LEAD: it is done for the whole horizontal scroll and, for the vertical ones, only after the scroll, for the re-home; the matching restore is the fill at $F1F6.

regions.name: East/west scroll: draw the incoming room into nametable 1
regions.description: $EFF3 with A = $24 draws the whole room (twelve 16-pixel bands from the room buffer $0740) into the nametable at PPU $2400, then a fill call. The incoming room is on screen first in NT1 while NT0 still holds the old one; the scroll then slides NT0 out and NT1 in.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 31 bytes of $FE at PPU $2301
regions.description: [count $1F][$23][$01][value $FE]: tile $FE across nametable 0 row 24 (the line at y = 192, where the HUD split fires), columns 1-31; column 0 is left to the room drawer. Read from the code; the picture of the row was not captured.

regions.name: East/west scroll: second marker row
regions.description: The fill call whose arguments follow.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 31 bytes of $FE at PPU $2701
regions.description: [count $1F][$27][$01][value $FE]: the same marker row in nametable 1 (row 24, columns 1-31).

regions.name: East/west scroll loop
regions.description: Waits one frame ($FFD1 with Y = 1: clear $2B and call the frame sync $DA9A Y times), then each frame: east ($A4 not 2) moves the ship's x down and adds 4 to the horizontal scroll $A8 (carrying into $A9 on the wrap); west ($A4 = 2) moves the ship up and subtracts 4 (the loop is the same shape). The ship's step is SBC #3 / ADC #3 with whatever carry the preceding LSRs left, so it ALTERNATES 3 and 4 pixels (a leftover of unused shifts). Then $E522 commits the scroll to the shadow registers and $F258 runs the ship's frame; it repeats until $A8 reaches 0 and jumps to the shared re-home at $F1DA. RUN, east exit from (y $78, x $D8): 79 frames with $A8/$A9 non-zero, $A8 = 4, 8, 12 ..., ship dx -3, -4, -3, -4 ... (220 px in all, from x 238 to 18), ending with ($A8, $A9) = (0, 1). CORRECTION: the Rendering page said the ship moves 3 px a frame; that is true of the vertical exits only.

regions.name: South scroll
regions.description: The south arm (A4 = 8). Sets $30 bit 4 (the NMI then moves the split marker tile with the scroll, as it does in a corridor), $AE = 12, $17 = $20, $16 = 0 (the room buffer offset of the band to draw: band 0 first), the record cursor $0440 = 0, and queues the first band through $F204. Then waits a frame and loops: every 16 pixels ($A6 AND $0F = 0) it draws the next band ($F204, $AE + 1, wrapping at 15 with $17 XOR 8 to switch between the $2000 and $2800 rows), the ship's y is reduced by 3 a frame (the room slides up past it), $A6 is increased by 4, then $E522 and $F258 run; until $A6 = $C0 (48 frames); then $F20A stores and flushes the last record and the shared tail runs at $F1B9. RUN, south exit: dispatch at frame 44, $A6 = 0 -> 192 in steps of 4, the ship's y 177 -> 33, 14 record stores and 12 flushes.

regions.name: North scroll
regions.description: The north arm (A4 = 0). Sets $30 bit 4, $AE = 14, $17:$16 = $28B0 ($16 doubles as the room-buffer offset of the band being drawn, $B0 = band 11, the BOTTOM band, since the new room enters from the top), waits one frame, then loops: every 16 pixels ($A6 AND $0F = 0) it waits for queue room ($E5EB), draws a band ($F03D, which also advances $16 by 16) and steps $16 down by $20 (net one band up) and $AE - 1; every frame the ship's y goes DOWN 3 ($0518 + 3), $A6 is reduced by 4 (the first step wraps 0 -> $EC and increments $A7, the nametable flip), $E522 commits the scroll and $F258 runs the ship's frame, until $A6 = $30. That is 48 frames and 12 bands. RUN, north exit from (y 14, x 120): dispatch at frame 26, $A6 = 236, 232, ... 48, ship y 14 -> 158, tail at frame 74.

regions.name: Vertical scroll finished: marker off, thin the split tile
regions.description: Shared by the north and south arms (the south arm jumps here). Clears $30 bit 4 (the NMI stops moving the marker) and makes the fill call whose arguments follow. Tile $FE is the solid split marker: plane 0 all $00, plane 1 all $FF. This clears plane-1 rows 2-7 ($1FEA-$1FEF), leaving only its first two scan lines opaque (measured: 00x8, ff ff 00 00 00 00 00 00). WHY is a LEAD: it is done for the whole horizontal scroll and, for the vertical ones, only after the scroll, for the re-home; the matching restore is the fill at $F1F6.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 6 bytes of $00 at PPU $1FEA
regions.description: [6][$1F][$EA][$00]. Tile $FE is the solid split marker: plane 0 all $00, plane 1 all $FF. This clears plane-1 rows 2-7 ($1FEA-$1FEF), leaving only its first two scan lines opaque (measured: 00x8, ff ff 00 00 00 00 00 00). WHY is a LEAD: it is done for the whole horizontal scroll and, for the vertical ones, only after the scroll, for the re-home; the matching restore is the fill at $F1F6.

regions.name: Vertical re-home, part 1: the new room into nametable 1
regions.description: Draws the incoming room into NT1 ($EFF3 with A = $24), zeroes the vertical scroll $A6/$A7 and the horizontal $A8, sets $A9 = 1 (the view points into NT1) and commits ($E522). The horizontal arm does NOT run this part (it jumps to $F1DA).

regions.name: Re-home, part 2: the room again into nametable 0, scroll to zero
regions.description: Shared with the horizontal arm. Draws the room into NT0 ($EFF3 with A = $20) FROM THE ROOM BUFFER (a redraw, not a copy), zeroes $A8, $A9, $A6, $A7 so the view returns to NT0 at scroll 0, commits ($E522), then the fill call below. CORRECTION: the Rendering page said the east/west re-home copies NT1 to NT0; the code redraws the room.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 32 blanks at PPU $2700
regions.description: [count $20][$27][$00][value $20]: blanks nametable 1 row 24, the HUD's blank top row.

regions.name: Re-home: restore the split tile
regions.description: The fill call whose arguments follow.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 6 bytes of $FF at PPU $1FEA
regions.description: [6][$1F][$EA][$FF]: restores plane-1 rows 2-7 of tile $FE (measured: back to ff x8). Undoes the fill at $F0AB / $F1C2.

regions.name: Re-home: blank nametable 1 row 0
regions.description: The fill call whose arguments follow.

regions.name: Fill arguments: 32 blanks at PPU $2400
regions.description: [count $20][$24][$00][value $20]: blanks the top row of nametable 1, left over from the incoming room.

regions.name: Room change: build the cell classes
regions.description: JMP $8006: a tail call to bank 5 $8354, which builds the new room's class map $0400-$045F from the room buffer. Its RTS returns to the caller of $F09A. RUN: reached 29 frames after the vertical tail ($F1B9) at frame 74 (north) and 92 (south).

regions.name: South scroll: queue a band, and re-queue its first column two calls later
regions.description: Called once per 16-pixel band by the south arm. Waits for queue room ($E5EB), draws the band ($F03D), then stores a 4-byte record at $0400 + the cursor $0440: the PPU address $AD:$AC and the first tile of each of the two tile rows ($0130, $0150, column 0). When the cursor is 8 or more it queues the record from two calls ago as a 2-tile VERTICAL run ([$82][hi][lo][t1][t2], increment 32) and advances the cursor by 4 either way. $F20A is the second entry, which skips the draw. OBSERVED in the south exit: the flushed addresses were $2300, $2340, $2380, $2800, $2840, $2880, $28C0, $2900 ... (column 0, row pairs), the tiles $9B $9B, $9B $8D, $82 $92 ..., 14 stores and 12 flushes. WHY the south scroll needs column 0 rewritten two bands late (the scratch buffer is the class map area $0400, which is rebuilt at $F201) is a LEAD; the north arm has no such step.

regions.name: One frame of a room scroll: only the ship
regions.description: Resets the sprite allocator ($CDB4: $80 = 4, the flags), then far-calls bank 3 $8003 -> $8F89 with X = 0: the ship's animation step (a phase counter from $C0A5, the base tile $06C8 from the table at $8F13 indexed by the facing and phase, metasprite $50, attributes from $8F33). Nothing else is processed during a room change.

regions.name: Far-call arguments: bank 3, target $8003
regions.description: [3][$02][$80]: bank 3 and the address minus one, $8002 + 1 = $8003 (the jump-table slot to $8F89).

regions.name: Draw the ship and finish the sprite list
regions.description: JSR $CBFC draws object X (the ship) with the metasprite machinery, then JMP $CE88: the sprite finish (hide stale sprites, flip the fill direction when needed).

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): the ship's entry point (`$F269`)
regions.description: The ship's x := `$F278[$A4]` and y := `$F279[$A4]`, `$A4` being the exit just used (0 N, 2 W, 4 none, 6 E, 8 S): **N (`78`, `90`), W (`DC`, `70`), none (`80`, `90`), E (`28`, `70`), S (`78`, `38`)** - the ship appears on the side opposite the exit.

regions.name: Table, 1 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $F26B, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to next read base $F279, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Table, 9 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $F271, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $F282, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Corridor start: blank the screen, then choose
regions.description: Called by JSR $EC99 in the corridor loader ($EC8C/$EC94), which has read the corridor number from the room record, so bank 5 is live here. $EDD1 FADES the display to black: the 24 saved palette bytes $04D0-$04E7 and the backdrop $0180 are set to black and $EDBD steps the fade ($D950) every two frames until it is done (8 frames in the run), then interrupts off and rendering off ($D4C7: $A3 = 0, PPUMASK bits 3-4 cleared); $D4E3 clears the NMI-enable bit of PPUCTRL. Then: corridor 0 or 22 go to the short path at $F290; every other corridor goes on to $F2A0. (Entry points inside this routine - $F2BB, $F2D9, $F336, $F43C, $F452 - are used by the stage-clear code too.)

regions.name: No flight: load the launch sprites and go straight on
regions.description: Taken by corridors 0 and 22 and by EVERY corridor of a TGL game (from $F2AE), so those never see the launch scene: $0680 = 0, $F6E5 loads the ship's sprite sheet (the decompressor armed with block 5 of bank 2 for PPU $0000), sprite 0's y is set to $BF (191, the HUD split) and it jumps to the tail at $F452. RUN: corridors 0 and 22, and all 23 TGL corridors, reached $F290; corridors 1-21 of a normal game reached $F2B4.

regions.name: The HUD's area number: fold the corridor onto the labyrinth
regions.description: $50 = the corridor folded onto the labyrinth's 1-10: 11-20 give 1-10 (CMP #$0B / SBC #$0A) and 21 is capped at 10. This is how leaving a corridor 'sets the area' (the labyrinth's HUD prints $50).

regions.name: TGL games skip the flight
regions.description: $30 bit 1 set (the TGL game) branches back to $F290.

regions.name: Launch jingle
regions.description: Plays sound $1D ($D852). The sound's identity was not looked up.

regions.name: Set the mode, load the launch sprites and the common scenes
regions.description: $F2B9 loads A = 0 and $F2BB stores A in $0680 - slot 0's field 16, used here as the MODE: 0 = taking off (the entry from $F2B9), 1 = landing (the stage-clear code at $F6BE jumps into $F2BB with A = 1). Then $F6E5 (the launch sprite sheet), $30 |= $48 (corridor mode and bit 3), and the bank 5 scene loader $8000 twice with A = 0 and A = $20: the two common scenes 0 and 32 (the blue panel tunnel, the same for every corridor), then waits for the decompressor ($D7C3) and switches to bank 4. HARNESS LESSON: the loader calls $8000 in the LIVE bank, so bank 5 must be live (as it is when $EC8C has just read the map record); from a savestate whose bank is 6 the call lands in bank 6, far-calls the ship's handler and bumps $0680, which made every start look like mode 1.

regions.name: Choose and start the flight's screen-data block
regions.description: A = $FF; only when $0680 is not 0 AND the corridor is 21 does it play sound $2D and use A = $FE. Bank 4's entry ($8000 -> $8003) takes entry number A + 2 of its pointer table: $FF -> entry 1 = $81ED (the flight block: scroll speed $0600 at once = 6 px a frame, a background row table, a palette list, three overlay records, no enemy wave), $FE -> entry 0 = $826D (a longer block: speed $0400 and then $1000). So entry 1 serves both modes and corridors 1-20; entry 0 is used only when landing from corridor 21. CORRECTION: this said the stage-clear code does not appear to reach it; it does - corridor 21's clear goes $F506 -> $F6B8 -> $F2BB with $51 = 21, plays sound $2D and runs entry 0 (RUN: a landing 1,061 frames long, against 352 for the other corridors). $E560 and $E5BD then start the stream engine on that block exactly as for a corridor. The parser calls these table entries 'area -2' and 'area -1'.

regions.name: The flight's ship: a type-$05 object in slot 0
regions.description: Slot 0 becomes type $05 with tile base $06C8 = 0, drawing flags $0620 = 1, target $0668 = 0 and thrust $0788 = 0. Mode 0: y = $30, y velocity +0.5 px a frame ($05D8 = 0, $05C0 = $80). Mode 1: y = $C8, velocity -0.25 ($05D8 = $FF, $05C0 = $C0). x = $80. RUN: corridors 1-21 of a normal game all gave y 48, velocity 0 . $80 at this point (the end of the routine's set-up).

regions.name: Reset the animation phase and switch the display on
regions.description: $CD99 clears the phase counter ($0638 whole, $0650 fraction), then A = $BF (sprite 0's y) and $EDE5: the sprite-0 set-up ($D51E), $05 and $4010 = $87 (the DMC rate), a wait for the vblank edges, NMI on ($D4F3), two frames' wait, rendering on ($D4D5), interrupts on.

regions.name: Flight loop: scroll, reset the sprites, pick the mode
regions.description: $E66A is the scroll step with the speed ramp (the stage step's speed code: $E530, then $B8/$B9 moved toward the target $BA/$BB), $CDB4 resets the sprite allocator, X = 0 (the ship), and $0680 = 0 branches to the mode-0 motion at $F3A7, otherwise it continues with the mode-1 motion.

regions.name: Landing (mode 1): the ship's pose and thrust from the phase
regions.description: Corridor 21: the y fraction $05C0 is set to $C4 and pose 1 is held (the phase is not advanced). Other corridors: the phase advances by $80 per frame while it is below $3C and by $60 after ($CD7A, wrapping at $C8). Phase below $60: the pose cycles through $F47B[phase mod 12] (ids 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 6 5 4 3 2; $F9AE is an 8-bit division, Y = Y mod A) with the attribute $F487 (bit 6 = flipped for the middle poses), no thrust. $60 to $6B: ids 1, 2, 3, 4, then 14, 15 ... 21 read backwards from $F46F, attribute $40, thrust $0788 = 8 (accelerating up through $CD12). From $6C: id 22, thrust 8. RUN, mode 1: ids 3, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 6, 5 ... from frame 79 at y 200 rising 0.25 px a frame, then the big shapes at the end; the ship leaves the top at frame 386.

regions.name: Take-off (mode 0): the ship's pose and thrust from the phase
regions.description: The phase steps by $30 while it is below $22 and by $60 from then on. Phase below 10: pose 22. 10-18: ids 22 down to 14 ($F46F[phase - 10]) then 4, 3, 2 (phases 19-21). From 22 to 69: $F47B[(phase - 10) mod 12] with the attribute $F487. From $46: pose 1 held. From phase $40 the thrust $0788 = $20 and the ship accelerates upward through $CD12 with that value (target y = 0 in $0668). RUN, mode 0: ids 22 (frames 26-84), 21 ... 14 (84-127), 4 3 2 1, then 2 ... 7 ... 1 repeating; y 48 -> 172 at +0.5 a frame, thrust $20 from frame ~285, off the top at frame 344.

regions.name: Draw the ship and its flame, then loop or leave
regions.description: $CBE8 draws object 0 (it returns carry set once the ship has left the screen). While the ship is rising ($05D8 negative) and its pose is below 14 it also draws metasprite $1D (the exhaust flame) with tile base $32 or $34 by bit 1 of the frame counter $41. $CE88 finishes the sprites. The loop ends when the ship is gone, or when SELECT IS HELD with no new press: $F493 handles a NEW Start (pause) or Select (the status screen), then $F7 bit 5 (Select held) exits. Otherwise one frame's wait ($FFD1 with Y = 1) and back to $F33E. RUN: a Select tap opens the status screen inside the scene (frame 60) and a second tap closes it and the scene resumes and ends later (413, not 344); Select held from before the scene starts leaves at the first pass (frame 26).

regions.name: Leave the flight: mode 0 loads the corridor's sprites and returns
regions.description: $EDD1 fades the screen to black and $F43C ($D755: bank 5) is also the entry the corridor-0 stage-clear code uses. Mode 1 goes to $F458. Mode 0: $30 bit 3 cleared, a 20-frame wait, the NMI off, then (also the target of $F290's shortcut) $F717 and $F705, which arm the decompressor for further sprite tiles from bank 2 (a block to PPU $0680 and one chosen from the selected weapon $3C in $F717, block $0C to $0740 in $F705; not read through) and wait for it ($D7C3); their return is this routine's return to $EC9C, where $EF6C begins the corridor proper. RUN: the exit at frame 344, the tail at 372.

regions.name: Leave the landing: back to the labyrinth's sprites
regions.description: Mode 1's tail: $30 bits 3 and 4 cleared, the first two bytes of slot 0's hit box ($06E0, $06F8) zeroed, and unless it is a TGL game $F6F5 loads the labyrinth ship's sprite sheet (bank 2 block 4 for PPU $0000) before $F717. Reached from the stage-clear code at $F6BE (a normal game, through the whole landing flight) and at $F659-$F664 (corridor 0's end, which jumps to $F43C and so skips the flight).

regions.name: Table, 12 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $F396, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $F47B, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Table, 12 bytes
regions.description: A table of 12 bytes at $F47B, read by LDA aby at $F379. THE EXTENT COMES FROM THE CODE, not from the data: the same routine reads another table based at $F487 from $F373, 6 bytes away in the instruction stream, so this table runs exactly up to that base. Two bases read by unrelated code would bound nothing, which is why the reads have to be neighbours. **WHAT THE BYTES MEAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED** - this region claims the extent and the reader and stops there. Generated by tools/find-tables.py.

regions.name: Table, 12 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $F373, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $F493, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Read the pads, then the pause check
regions.description: Slot $C16B; called once per game-loop pass ($FF92), by the launch flight loop, the stage-clear loops and the key-panel wait. $D64C reads the pads (so $F5/$F6 hold new presses, $F7/$F8 held buttons); if $30 bit 7 is clear (not a demo) it jumps to the pause/status routine $E4B3, whose RTS returns to the caller.

regions.name: Demo: a new Start ends it
regions.description: In a demo ($30 bit 7) a new Start press ($F5 bit 4) jumps to $FF4A (the game's start-up, i.e. leaves the attract mode); anything else returns. The pause routine is not reachable in a demo.

regions.name: Which key does this corridor award?
regions.description: In: $51. Out: A = the key number (Z set when none). Corridor 0 and every corridor from 11 up: 0; corridors 1-10: $F6DA[corridor] (the table at $F6DB, read one byte early because the index starts at 1) = 1 2 3 4 0 5 0 6 7 0. Called by the stage-clear code only.

regions.name: Scripted ship entrance on the cleared-corridor gate screen
regions.description: Called from $EC4C when the labyrinth's special screen type $51 is 5 (the gate once its corridor is cleared; $EC43).
