Sets slot 0 to type $81 (the player's type $01 with bit 7 set), metasprite $50, flags $03, x $70, y $C8, y velocity and target $FB (-5), the state counter $07E8 = 2, then (bank 6 selected) loops one frame at a time - pads ($F493) and one object-loop pass ($8000) - until $07E8 reaches 0. RUN from a corridor savestate (so the room is not the real one): it returned after 420 frames with $07E8 stepping 2 -> 3 -> 0 and the ship ending near (152, 202). What the type-$81 ship does with its state counter, and the screen it plays on, were not worked out (LEAD).

regions.name: STAGE CLEAR: the jingle
regions.description: Entered by JSR from the stage-end code $ECBD (corridor 21 at $ECC7, 22 at $ECE1, corridors 0-20 at $ECE7 - 1-20 after marking the corridor cleared, $EFBA). Plays sound $17 (the clear jingle; id not looked up) unless the corridor is 0 or 22, then selects bank 6.

regions.name: Stage clear: stop the spawning, run the scroll down to a stop
regions.description: $60 low two bits cleared (the spawn script stops), $A0 bit 0 cleared (the end-of-stage request that brought us here), then loops: speed target $BA/$BB = 0, the scroll step and speed ramp ($E66A: 2/256 a frame), one full game-loop pass ($FF8B: the ship, shots and enemies keep running) until the speed $B8/$B9 is 0. RUN: it takes speed / 2 frames - 19 for corridor 4 (speed 38), 20 for 21, 1,264 for corridor 0 (speed 2,528, the Defense System's stage).

regions.name: Stage clear: clear the objects, then the key if there is one
regions.description: $EA68 removes objects 1-23. A TGL game ($30 bit 1) goes straight to the flight at $F5DE; otherwise $F4A7 gives the corridor's key and none (corridors 0, 5, 7, 10, 11 and up) goes there too.

regions.name: Stage clear: award the key
regions.description: Y = the key number: bit (key - 1) is ORed into the key inventory $04B0 (the mask table at $EFD8, read from $EFD7 + key), sound $36 plays, $19:$18 = $15C0 (the pattern-table address the key's icon is built at) and A = the key number goes to the icon builder: far call to bank 2 slot $8006 (-> $8212; the 3 inline bytes follow at $F566). RUN, corridor 4: $04B0 went $00 -> $08 at frame 18, sound $36 at 18.

regions.name: Far-call argument at $F566
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $F563 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 2 $8006**. The stored word is $8005 rather than $8006 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Key panel: paint a black 10 x 3 block of metatile $20
regions.description: Cells x = $30, $40 ... $C0 by y = $40, $50, $60 (pixel positions, 10 columns x 3 rows) are each filled with metatile $20 through $FAB7 (the block-redraw routine behind $FA96: it adds the scroll $A6 to y, wrapping at $F0, converts the position to a PPU address and queues the tiles; in a corridor, $30 bit 6, it skips the labyrinth's class write). The result is a plain black rectangle over the corridor (picture from the run).

regions.name: Key panel: the icon's cell
regions.description: One more $FAB7 call with metatile $5C at (x $B0, y $50): the cell the key's icon sprite sits in.

regions.name: Key panel: the text position and the message
regions.description: $19:$18 = (x $40, y $50 + scroll, wrapped and masked to a tile row) converted by $FA6B to a PPU address, then JSR $D53F with the inline string ' YOU GOT KEY' (12 characters, at $F5CC): the line is written at column 8 of the panel's middle row. RUN: the picture shows the black panel, YOU GOT KEY and the key icon.

regions.name: " YOU GOT KEY" at $F5CC
regions.description: A queued PPU write item, written inline after `JSR $D53F` at bank 7 $F5C9. Its shape is [count][count characters]: unlike $D576 this routine takes the PPU address from $18/$19 in RAM rather than from the stream, which is what makes its block two bytes shorter. The block is 13 bytes and the caller resumes immediately after it; the length comes from the first byte by the rule in $D591 - (byte & $7F) + 3 below $C0, 9 at or above - and $D5A5 advances the routine's own pointer by exactly that. It reads " YOU GOT KEY". Characters are ASCII for the letters and space. NOT ESTABLISHED: the glyphs for codes outside A-Z and space, which only the font can settle - and no font has been found yet, because CHR is RAM on this cartridge.

regions.name: Key panel: hold for 40 game-loop passes
regions.description: LDY #$28 / JSR $FF8B: 40 passes (43 frames from the award to the flight in the run), then falls into the flight.

regions.name: The ship flies away: set it up
regions.description: Slot 0 becomes type 5 (the flight ship), metasprite 1, $0560, tile base $06C8, phase $0638 and the y fraction cleared. Corridors 0 and 22: phase 1 at once and velocity/target 0 (it will climb); every other corridor: phase 0, y velocity and target $0668 = $FE, flags $0620 = 5.

regions.name: The ship flies away: phase 0 (normal corridors)
regions.description: Each pass: a game-loop pass ($FF8B, Y = 1), pads, sprite reset ($CDB4), X = 0. Phase 0: when y is below $20 it applies thrust $0C toward the target ($CD12), draws the ship ($CBE8; carry = it has left the screen) and, when it has, steps the phase, y := 0, y fraction and velocity := 0. RUN (corridor 4): the ship climbs at 2 px a frame from y 160, left the top at frame 85 of the flight and re-appeared at y 0 as phase 1.

regions.name: The ship flies away: phase 1
regions.description: Thrust $20 toward the target $0668, draw, and leave the loop when the ship is off the screen. Target $0668 = $FE for normal corridors, so the ship comes in again from the top and DIVES, accelerating (y velocity 3, 6, 7 px a frame; off the bottom 57 frames later); target 0 for corridors 0 and 22, so from its place on the screen it climbs off the top (51 frames in corridor 0).

regions.name: The ship is gone: corridor 0 (and TGL) end here
regions.description: $CE88 finishes the sprites; corridor 0 (and the TGL path from $F6B2) sets $0680 = 1 (landing mode), fades out ($EDD1), turns the screen off ($D4E3) and jumps to the landing tail $F43C: no landing flight. Corridor 22 goes on at $F667, all others at $F6B2.

regions.name: Corridor 22: the final score screen (set-up)
regions.description: Fade out, hide all sprites ($D534: $F8 to every OAM byte), screen off, sound $1F, scroll zeroed ($D4FD), nametable 0 blanked ($E445 with A = $20), wait for the decompressor, then the inline string 'YOUR FINAL SCORE' at PPU $2086.

regions.name: "YOUR FINAL SCORE" at $F687
regions.description: A queued PPU write item, written inline after `JSR $D576` at bank 7 $F684. Its shape is [count][ppu_hi][ppu_lo][count characters]: the destination $2086 is in the block itself. The block is 19 bytes and the caller resumes immediately after it; the length comes from the first byte by the rule in $D591 - (byte & $7F) + 3 below $C0, 9 at or above - and $D5A5 advances the routine's own pointer by exactly that. It reads "YOUR FINAL SCORE". Characters are ASCII for the letters and space. NOT ESTABLISHED: the glyphs for codes outside A-Z and space, which only the font can settle - and no font has been found yet, because CHR is RAM on this cartridge.

regions.name: Final score: the fixed trailing zero
regions.description: A second inline string, a single '0' at PPU $20CE: the score is kept in tens, so the screen prints a constant 0 after its six digits.

regions.name: "0" at $F69D
regions.description: A queued PPU write item, written inline after `JSR $D576` at bank 7 $F69A. Its shape is [count][ppu_hi][ppu_lo][count characters]: the destination $20CE is in the block itself. The block is 4 bytes and the caller resumes immediately after it; the length comes from the first byte by the rule in $D591 - (byte & $7F) + 3 below $C0, 9 at or above - and $D5A5 advances the routine's own pointer by exactly that. It reads "0". Characters are ASCII for the letters and space. NOT ESTABLISHED: the glyphs for codes outside A-Z and space, which only the font can settle - and no font has been found yet, because CHR is RAM on this cartridge.

regions.name: Final score: print the digits, then the ending
regions.description: $19:$18 = $20C8 and $E118 prints the six score digits ($0170-$0175, leading zeros blanked); then the far call to bank 2 slot $8021 (-> $8A69, the ending; it never returns - see the ending notes).

regions.name: Far-call argument at $F6AF
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $F6AC - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 2 $8021**. The stored word is $8020 rather than $8021 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: Normal corridors: fade out and start the LANDING flight
regions.description: TGL games take $F659 (no flight). Otherwise: fade ($EDD1), bank 5, A = 1 and JMP $F2BB, the launch routine with the mode set to 1 - the landing flight - whose RTS returns to the caller of $F506. RUN: corridor 4 flew from $F6B8 at frame 203 to $F2BB at 211 and the landing finished 352 frames later; **corridor 21 takes the same path and DOES reach the 'entry 0' block**: sound $2D and bank 4 entry 0 ($826D), a landing 1,061 frames long (CORRECTION: the launch-flight notes called this unreached).

regions.name: The ship's exhaust flame
regions.description: $0788 counts frames; tile base $87 = $32 + ($0788 AND 2) (alternating $32 / $34), metasprite $1D drawn with $CC34 at the ship, then $CE88 and back to the loop at $F612. The same flame the launch flight draws.

regions.name: Key awarded by corridors 1-10
regions.description: $F4A7: LDY $51 (the corridor) / BEQ / CPY #$0B / BCC - so corridors 1-10 only - LDA $F6DA,Y. $F4B7 passes the same value to the far call to bank 2 $8006, the key-icon builder, after LDA #$81 / STA $0500 / ORA $04B0 / STA $04B0 on the key inventory. Values 1 2 3 4 0 5 0 6 7 0. Checked against the world map: corridor n gives the key that labyrinth area n+1 needs (areas 1-10 need 0,1,2,3,4,4,5,5,6,7), and corridors 5, 7 and 10 give none because the next area needs a key already held.

regions.name: Load the corridor ship's sprite sheet
regions.description: $19:$18 = 0 (PPU $0000), block 5 of bank 2 armed for the decompressor ($D7F9) and waited for. Callers: $ECD0, $F295, $F2BE. RUN.

regions.name: Load the labyrinth ship's sprite sheet
regions.description: Block 4 of bank 2 to PPU $0000. Callers: $EB66 and the landing tail $F468. RUN.

regions.name: Load block $0C of bank 2 to PPU $0740
regions.description: The common sprite tiles of the corridors (what they hold was not drawn). Reached by JMP from $F455 at the end of a launch. RUN.

regions.name: Load the sprite tiles for the selected weapon
regions.description: Block 6 of bank 2 to PPU $0680 always, then by the weapon $3C and its level $3D: tables $F77F (0 none, 1/2 a level threshold, $FF the beam), $F772 (the block) and $F78B (the beam's block by level). RUN, every weapon x level 0-3: no weapon or the Enemy Eraser (12): nothing more; 1 MultiBullets, 4 Bullet Shield, 8 Repeller: block 7 at $0760, but block $0A at $0780 instead at level 3; 6 Fireball the same from level 2; 2 Back Fire and 3 Wave Attack: block $0B at $0760; 5 Grenade: $0A at $0780 and 8 at $0760; 7, 10, 11: block 7 at $0760; 9 Hyper Laser: blocks $1E, $1F, $20 at $0760 for levels 1-3 (none at 0). Callers: $EB69, $ECD3, $F452 and by JMP $F46B.

regions.name: Table, 13 bytes
regions.description: A table of 13 bytes at $F772, read by LDA aby at $F74C. THE EXTENT COMES FROM THE CODE, not from the data: the same routine reads another table based at $F77F from $F730, 28 bytes away in the instruction stream, so this table runs exactly up to that base. Two bases read by unrelated code would bound nothing, which is why the reads have to be neighbours. **WHAT THE BYTES MEAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED** - this region claims the extent and the reader and stops there. Generated by tools/find-tables.py.

regions.name: Table, 12 bytes
regions.description: A table of 12 bytes at $F77F, read by LDA aby at $F730. THE EXTENT COMES FROM THE CODE, not from the data: the same routine reads another table based at $F78B from $F747, 23 bytes away in the instruction stream, so this table runs exactly up to that base. Two bases read by unrelated code would bound nothing, which is why the reads have to be neighbours. **WHAT THE BYTES MEAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED** - this region claims the extent and the reader and stops there. Generated by tools/find-tables.py.

regions.name: Table, 4 bytes (structural extent)
regions.description: A table read by LDA aby at $F747, starting at the first byte of an unclaimed stretch. ITS EXTENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATED BY THE CODE: it runs to the claimed byte at $F78F, because nothing else claims the bytes in between. A LEAD - the reader's index range has not been checked. Generated by tools/find-tables.py (second rule).

regions.name: Spawn-script interpreter: select the script's bank
regions.description: Called from one place, $E998 in the loader/spawn entry $E995 (after the art-load step, with the caller's bank on the stack), once per stage step. $7F = the bank that holds the script: 5 for a labyrinth room's script, 4 for a corridor wave script (stream command 2 sets it). The script pointer is $66/$67 and the wait counter $68; $60 bit 1 = a script is running, bit 3 = spawning is stopped (a boss fight).

regions.name: Interpreter: is it time for a tick?
regions.description: No script running ($60 bit 1 clear) -> return. LABYRINTH ($30 bit 6 clear), or a corridor whose scroll speed $B8/$B9 is 0: $69 is decremented once per call and reaches 0 every 60 calls, so the script advances once a second (frames). A corridor that is scrolling advances once per NEW BACKGROUND ROW instead ($A0 bit 2, set when a row is built and cleared by the next stage step). RUN: a corridor script with no new row never advanced; with a row each call it advanced every call; a stopped corridor counted $69 like the labyrinth. RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Interpreter: a tick - count the wait, fetch the next item
regions.description: $69 = 60 for the next second, Y = 0; $68 is decremented and the script returns until it reaches 0 (so a wait of N is N ticks; a wait of 0 wraps to 255 and lasts 256 ticks - RUN). Then the next byte of the script: Y + 1 -> $15 (the offset of its operands); a value under 3 is a command, anything else a spawn (-> $F7F4). RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Command dispatch
regions.description: JSR $D6AE: the inline jump table that follows ($F7C9, three entries): 0 wait, 1 jump, 2 end.

regions.name: Spawn-script commands: 3 entries
regions.description: Inline jump table after JSR $D6AE at $F7C6 in the spawn-script interpreter: 0 wait, 1 jump, 2 end. CMP #$03 / BCS before it bounds the index. Registered in annotations/dispatch.json.

regions.name: Script command 0: wait
regions.description: One operand byte -> $68 (the number of ticks to wait; ticks are seconds in the labyrinth and rows in a scrolling corridor), then $F852 saves the pointer and returns. RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Script command 1: jump
regions.description: Two operand bytes (low, high) -> the script pointer $66/$67 and the next item is fetched AT ONCE, in the same tick (Y = 0, JMP $F7BD): a loop with no wait in it would never return, and the five labyrinth scripts that jump into non-script memory carry on reading there. RUN: a one-spawn loop spawned once per tick. RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Script command 2: end
regions.description: $60 bit 1 cleared: the script is finished and the routine returns without a tick from then on. RUN: running = 0 from the next call.

regions.name: Spawn item: skip it while spawning is stopped
regions.description: A byte of 3 or more is a type to spawn, $80 and up a FORMATION of the type in its low seven bits. If $60 bit 3 is set (spawning stopped, copied from the boss's $71 at the boss start) nothing is created: a plain type has no operands, a formation's two operand bytes (count, interval) are skipped, and the delay that follows is still honoured. RUN.

regions.name: Spawn item: allocate a slot
regions.description: A plain type takes the LOWEST free slot from 5 up ($FA5B: it only looks, never reclaims; the code switches to bank 6 around the call and back to $7F for no visible reason). A formation uses the allocator $EA8C, which takes the HIGHEST free slot and can reclaim one. If there is no slot the item is dropped exactly as when spawning is stopped (the operands are skipped, the delay honoured). RUN: the first plain spawn went to slot 5, a formation to slot 23; with every slot full both were lost and the script went on.

regions.name: Spawn item: fill the new object
regions.description: A plain spawn stores only the type in $0500,X (the handler sets everything else on its first frame). A formation stores a TYPE-$29 SPAWNER: the formation's type in its metasprite field $0548, the count in $0560 and the interval in $07A0 (read from the two operand bytes), type $29 in $0500; the spawner (bank 6 $9A19) then makes the objects one per interval. RUN: [$91 04 05] gave a $29 object with $0548 = $11, count 4, interval 5.

regions.name: Spawn item: the delay after it
regions.description: The next byte is the DELAY, not a command: a value with bit 7 set is instead the next spawn item (several enemies on the same tick), handled again from $F7F4; otherwise it goes to $68 and the script returns, to act again that many ticks later. A delay of 0 is special: it does not wait, it SKIPS the following byte and carries straight on in the same tick (RUN: the byte after the zero was ignored and the next item spawned on the same tick). No bank 5 script has a zero delay; one bank 4 corridor script has (and one has a wait 0: the tail of corridor 16, see its entry).

regions.name: Interpreter: save the script pointer
regions.description: Adds Y (the bytes read this tick) to $66/$67 and returns; the caller restores the bank.

regions.name: Aim at the player and fly that way
regions.description: Slot $C0FC. $F863 (the direction to slot 0) and then $F8CE (turn that direction into a velocity for object X): the bullet and homing-enemy idiom. Called from $FE71 and through the slot. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Aim: the vertical distance
regions.description: Slot $C0FF. In: X = the shooter, Y = 0 (the target is slot 0, the player's ship). $38 = 0 collects flags. dy = $0518,Y - $0518,X is made positive in $10 (flag $04 when the target is ABOVE, i.e. negative) and a zero becomes 1, so the division below never has a zero. Positions are the objects' own y and x fields, not their centres. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Aim: the horizontal distance
regions.description: The same for x into $11: flag $08 when the target is to the LEFT; zero becomes 1.

regions.name: Aim: put the larger distance first
regions.description: If |dx| >= |dy| the two are swapped (so $10 is always the larger, $11 the smaller) and flag $10 is set: the line is more horizontal than vertical.

regions.name: Aim: the angle from a ratio, then the direction
regions.description: $F9B6 computes smaller x 256 / larger (tan of the angle off the major axis, 0-255). It is compared with the three thresholds at $F95B ($AB, $6A, $32 = tan 33.75, 22.5 and 11.25 degrees x 256, tried from the smallest) giving Y = 3 (within 11.25 degrees of the axis) down to 0 (33.75 degrees or more); Y OR the flags indexes the 32-byte table $F95E, which holds the direction 0-15. Out: A = the direction (0 right, 4 down, 8 left, 12 up, 22.5 degrees each); X unchanged; Y = the table index, NOT preserved. RUN: the 16 directions come out at every 22.5 degrees; a 910-point grid matches an independent model built from the thresholds, and 529 offsets match 'nearest of 16 by atan2' with no difference; a target on top of the shooter gives 2 (down-right); a target in slot 3 works the same.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: the base vector
regions.description: Slot $C102. In: A = the direction (AND $0F), X = the object. Y is kept in $38. The 16-bit vector is built from the sine table: y = $F986[2 x dir] -> $12 (sign extended into $10) and x = $F98E[2 x dir] -> $13 (into $11), i.e. 120 x sin and 120 x cos of the direction in 1/256 pixel. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: the speed class scale
regions.description: The object's $0698: bit 7 multiplies the vector by 8 (three shifts), bit 6 by 4 (two more); both give 32. The low six bits are the multiplier applied next.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: add it count times
regions.description: Zeroes the object's velocity fields ($05C0/$05D8 y fraction/integer, $05F0/$0608 x) and adds the scaled vector (low six bits of $0698) times. A count of 0 returns BEFORE this, leaving the velocity as it was. So speed = 120 x scale x count / 256 pixels a frame: $0698 = $81 is 3.75, $43 5.62, $82 7.5, $83 11.25, $C1 15.0, $01 0.47, $7F 118 - the gun's speed classes. RUN, all of these.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: restore Y
regions.description: LDY $38 and RTS (also the end byte the table below is indexed from).

regions.name: Aiming thresholds
regions.description: $AB $6A $32 = tan(33.75), tan(22.5), tan(11.25) x 256 (171, 106 and 50; the exact values are 171.1, 106.0 and 50.9). Read as $F95A + Y for Y = 3, 2, 1: the base is the RTS byte before the table, the overlap trick again.

regions.name: Aiming: direction by flags and angle step
regions.description: 32 bytes in four groups of eight: index = flags ($04 target above, $08 target left, $10 more horizontal than vertical) + the step Y = 0-3 above. Not swapped (vertical major): down-right 2 3 3 4, up-right 14 13 13 12, down-left 6 5 5 4, up-left 10 11 11 12; swapped (horizontal major): 2 1 1 0, 14 15 15 0, 6 7 7 8, 10 9 9 8. Step 3 is the pure axis direction (4 down, 12 up, 0 right, 8 left), step 0 the diagonal.

regions.name: Sine lookup
regions.description: Slot $C0F6: A = $F986,Y: 120 x sin(11.25 degrees x Y) as a signed byte (Y 0-31). Callers: the orbiting weapon in bank 6 ($88A0, $88B7: the Bullet Shield's position round the ship from a 32-step phase, the result scaled down by arithmetic shifts). RUN: Y = 4, 8, 16, 24 gave 84, 120, 0, -120.

regions.name: Cosine lookup
regions.description: Slot $C0F9: A = $F98E,Y, the same table eight entries on (+90 degrees): 120 x cos. RUN: Y = 0 gave 120, 16 gave -120.

regions.name: Sine table: 120 x sin(11.25 degrees x k), k = 0-39
regions.description: 00 17 2d 42 54 63 6e 75 78 75 6e 63 54 42 2d 17 00 e9 d3 be ac 9d 92 8b 88 8b 92 9d ac be d3 e9 then 00 17 2d 42 54 63 6e 75 again: a full circle of 32 signed bytes (peak $78 = 120) and the first eight repeated so that cosine = the same table read eight entries (a quarter turn) later, up to k = 31 + 8. The direction routine reads every second entry (2 x direction); the odd ones serve the 32-step phase of the orbiting weapon. CORRECTION: this was claimed as an 8-byte table 'whose meaning is not established' and a 32-byte structural-extent lead.

regions.name: Divide: Y / A (entry 1)
regions.description: Slot $C10B. In: A = the divisor, Y = the dividend. Out: A = the quotient, Y = the remainder (the 8-bit restoring divide at $F9BD). Callers: $D2DF, and the launch flight's pose cycle ($F370, $F3DB, which use the remainder). RUN: 10/3 = 3 rem 1, 7/7 = 1 rem 0, 3/10 = 0 rem 3, 200/1 = 200.

regions.name: Divide: Y x 256 / A (entry 2, the aiming ratio)
regions.description: In: A = the divisor, Y = the numerator. The dividend is Y x 256, so the quotient is the fraction Y/A as 0-255 (for Y = A it gives 255, not 256: 100 x 256 / 100 returned 255 with remainder 100 on the model). Called only by the aiming code, where Y < A always except for equal distances. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Divide: the shift-and-subtract loop
regions.description: Eight rounds of: shift the dividend left through the accumulator, subtract the divisor when it fits and set the quotient bit in $11. Ends with TAY (the remainder), LDA $11 (the quotient).

regions.name: The random number: a mix of machine state
regions.description: Slot $C0EA (27 callers: banks 0, 1, 3 and 6, the demo's input timer $DAF4, the demo's corridor pick $EB53, the explosion box $FB27, $F9E9). In: nothing is required, but the result DEPENDS on A (and the carry), X, Y, the live bank and the stack depth. Out: A = the new $2A (also stored there); X and Y preserved ($10 holds X). The arithmetic, in order: A = ROL A (carry in); + $2A + carry; EOR the byte at $8000 + X (whichever bank is live: the ROM is an entropy source); + $0400,Y (RAM indexed by Y); EOR $0200 + the stack pointer (a sprite byte, indexed by how deep the stack is); + $2A + carry; - $41 (the frame counter) - borrow. So it is not a generator with a period of its own: it is stirred by the game's running state, and the DMC IRQ stirs $2A as well ($DCE8). RUN: 400 random states against a Python model of exactly this arithmetic: 0 differences (single-stepped; a frame run between would change $41 and the OAM). In 3,000 frames of play, one call per frame with A = X = Y = 0, all 256 values appeared, the top-nibble histogram was flat (162-213 per bin of 187.5 expected) and consecutive equal values occurred twice. With the machine frozen except $41 += 1 it gave 38 distinct values in 40 calls. Not established: how the sequence behaves on hardware, which has the IRQ stirring.

regions.name: Random x at the top of the screen
regions.description: Slot $C0F0 (17 callers in banks 3 and 6: enemies that enter from the top). In: X = the object. Out: x ($0530,X) = a random value, y ($0518,X) = 8; X and Y preserved. The x comes from $F9D1: a value from $20 to $DF is used as it is; a value under $20 or $E0 and over is folded to $20 + (v AND $1F) + 2 x (v AND $3F), 32-189. Then $2A is re-stirred with the zero-page byte at (x / 2). RUN, 3,000 calls: x from 32 to 223 (191 of the 192 values seen, no value outside $20-$DF), y always 8; the folded values make the middle bins a little heavier (509 against about 375).

regions.name: Random position in the playing field
regions.description: Slot $C0F3 (10 callers in bank 6). In: X = the object. Out: x as above ($F9E9), y ($0518,X) = a random value from $28 to $B7 built from a sprite byte ($0200,$2A), $2A and the x ($11 AND $7F + $12 AND $3F + $28, reduced by $90 when it reaches $B8); X preserved, Y = the new y (NOT preserved: the routine ends with TAY). $2A is re-stirred with another sprite byte. RUN, 3,000 calls: x 32-223, y 40-183 (the whole of $28-$B7), 1,265 distinct positions.

regions.name: Spawn an object at another object's position
regions.description: Slot $C105 (about 25 callers in banks 1, 3 and 6, and $FE3F). In: A = the type to create, X = the object whose position is copied (the parent), Y = the slot to fill (usually just found by $FA5B). Stores the type in $0500,Y and copies the parent's x ($0530) and y ($0518) into the new slot; nothing else is written, so the slot must be a free one, whose other fields were zeroed when it was freed ($CCBF), and the child's handler sets the rest on its first frame. Out: A = the parent's y, X and Y unchanged. RUN: A = $2B, X = 9 at (111, 77), Y = 12 gave type $2B at x 111, y 77 with the other fields left at 0. The usual sequence is $FA5B (find a slot) then this, then the caller sets velocity and other fields. Boss and enemy shots use it.

regions.name: Find a free enemy slot
regions.description: Entered through the jump-table slot $C108. Scans slots 5 to 23 for a type of 0 and returns the index in Y with carry clear, or carry set when all 19 are in use. Everything that spawns anything dynamic (explosions, sparks, the formation spawner, the script interpreter's spawns, blasts) goes through this or its sibling $EA8C, which can also reuse some occupied slots.

regions.name: Pixel position to nametable address
regions.description: Entered through the slot $C111. In: $19 = x, $18 = y (already adjusted for the scroll by the caller). Out: $19:$18 = the PPU address of the 8 x 8 tile that holds the point, $2000 + 32 x (y / 8) + x / 8 (high byte $20 + y / 64, low byte (y AND $F8) x 4 | x / 8), and Y = the matching attribute-table offset, $C0 | (y AND $E0) / 4 | x / 32 (the low byte of $23C0 + ...). The block-break routine at $FA96 passes it a point already rounded to a 16 x 16 cell.

regions.name: Break a block: blast, redraw, new cell class
regions.description: Entered through the slot $C117; callers are the weapon-hits-cell code (bank 6 $854B), the boss/stage routine (bank 3 $92B2, $9336) and bank 1 $8159. In: $19 = x, $18 = y of a point in the cell, $16 = the tile argument for the redraw, $15 = the cell's NEW class. It (1) allocates an object through $FA5B and makes it a type-$30 blast at the cell's centre ($19 AND $F0 | 8, $18 AND $F0 | 7); (2) adds the vertical scroll $A6 to y (wrapping at $F0), converts to a PPU address ($FA6B) and queues the new tiles through $D865 with $16; (3) restores $18/$19 and falls into the class write below. If no slot is free the blast is skipped (the BCS at $FA99 goes to $FAB7) but the tiles are still queued and the class still written. RUN on the labyrinth savestate with ($18, $19) = (100, 140) and $15 = 7: a type-$30 blast appeared at y 103, x 136, nine bytes were queued for the PPU, $18/$19 came back unchanged and the cell's class went 0 -> 7 without touching its neighbours. $FADE-$FB11, the class write, is also the jump-table slot $C11D on its own: in the labyrinth only (it does nothing when $30 bit 6 is set, a corridor, run) it stores $15 into the nibble of the class map $0400 for the cell at ($18, $19): index = (y AND $F0) / 2 | x / 32, and bit 4 of x chooses the low nibble (set) or the high one (clear).

regions.name: One explosion at a random point in a box
regions.description: Entered through the slot $C120; callers are bank 1 $80D0 (the boss-death barrage) and bank 2 $88EF (the planet cutscene). Allocates a slot ($FA5B; carry set if none), makes it a type-$08 explosion with $0740 = 0, and places it near ($19 = x, $18 = y) jittered by the box size ($15 wide, $14 high) using the random routine $F9D1, then plays sound $22 ($D852). RUN 300 times with $14 = 32, $15 = 48 at (y 100, x 128): one object per call, y 83-116, x 104-136, so the spread is about half the box size each way in y but skewed in x (the x offset comes from a rotated copy of the same random byte). Read from the code, not from a hardware picture.

regions.name: Negate the y velocity
regions.description: Slot $C126. 0 - ($05D8,X:$05C0,X): the 16-bit y velocity of the calling object (whole byte $05D8, fraction $05C0) is negated, i.e. the object bounces vertically. Callers: types $52 and $59 (bank 6 $A7EB, $B102). Read, not run.

regions.name: Negate the x velocity
regions.description: Slot $C123. 0 - ($0608,X:$05F0,X): the 16-bit x velocity of the calling object is negated, a horizontal bounce. Callers: types $5A and $52 (bank 6 $A5B7, $A7E8). Read, not run.

regions.name: A beam's head and tail: following its parent
regions.description: Slot $C129 (the first half). Called every frame by the Hyper Laser's run routine (weapon 9, bank 6 $8AC4) and by enemy type $22 (bank 6 $A0B8). Reads: $0668,X is the slot of a parent object and $0680,X the type that parent must keep (otherwise it returns with carry set and the caller ends the beam); $0788,X is a phase counter (the parent's x is copied into $0530,X while $0788 is below $0620,X; $0788 is set to 2 at $FBA8 and incremented at $FBC5 and $FBE4); the head is $0518,X, tested against the y velocity ($05D8,X) through $FCC3/$FCCD (beyond $D0 means off the top); $0758,X is the other end of the beam, written at $FBF7 and read by the drawing half. The branches that choose between growing, holding and ending were not worked through, so this region is a LEAD; the drawing half below was run.

regions.name: A beam: a column of sprites, and its hit box
regions.description: The second half of slot $C129. Draws a vertical chain between the object's two y ends ($0518,X and $0758,X) in steps of 16 pixels, one piece per step: the object's metasprite $0548,X through $CC34, or, when that is 0, single sprites through $CF05, at x $0530,X with attributes $0560,X and base tile $06C8,X. It then sets the collision box that $D348 reads: x from $0530 - $0650 to $0530 + $0650 (clamped to 0 and 255) into $06E0/$06F8, and y from the smaller end to the larger + 15 into $0710/$0728. $0650,X is the beam's half-width. RUN as the Hyper Laser (weapon 9) from the corridor savestate: the routine was entered once per frame while the beam lived; the box half-widths were 3, 8 and 24 pixels (widths 6, 16, 48) at levels 1, 2 and 3 and the y extent ran from the beam's head (y 128 -> 68 as it rose at level 1) to a second end (147 at level 1, 191 at levels 2 and 3 in the frames sampled); level 1 drew single sprites (at x - 4), levels 2 and 3 metasprites 26 and 23.

regions.name: Beam helpers: y plus velocity, and a +/-16 wrap
regions.description: $FCC3: A + the y velocity's whole byte ($05D8,X), compared with $D0; returns Y = that velocity (carry set = beyond $D0). $FCCD (entered with the flags $FCC3 left, so N = the velocity's sign): a positive velocity subtracts 16 (SBC #$10), a negative one adds 15 plus carry ($FCD2, ADC #$0F): moves a beam end by one 16-pixel piece against the direction it travels. Called only from the beam routine.

regions.name: Move with the scroll
regions.description: Slot $C12C. In a corridor ($30 bit 6) adds the scroll step $B7 (whole pixels moved this frame) to the object's y $0518,X, so the object stays fixed on the background; returns carry set when the result passes $D0 (off the bottom). In the labyrinth it does nothing. Callers: the pickup box (bank 2 $8543) and ground types $16, $63 and $7A (bank 6 $8C24, $AFF4, $BA56, $BA5E). Read, not run.

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): add chips (`$FCE7`, slot `$C12F`)
regions.description: Chips `$4D:$4C` += A; overflow or above the maximum `$4F:$4E` clamps to the maximum; then `JSR $FD77` (the selected weapon's level and cost), `JSR $E1C3` (print the uses left) and `JMP $E213` (the gun tier and the chip counter).

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): attack, shield and speed (`$FD0E`, slot `$C132`)
regions.description: **The ship's attack `$05A8` := `$FD4A[$4A]` = 1, 2, 3, 5 for attack levels 1-4 (capped at 4). `$0590` (the damage divisor) := the shield level `$4B` (capped at 7).** A shield level of 0 gives attack 64, divisor 32. **The speed class `$0698` := `$FD4F[i]` = `03 05 41 06` with i = 0 for shield under 5, 2 for 5 or more, +1 in a corridor: so a shield of level 5 or more speeds the ship up (labyrinth class 3 -> `$41`, corridor 5 -> 6).** RUN: all of it.

regions.name: Player attack by attack level, and a value by mode
regions.description: $FD0E: LDY $4A / CPY #$04 / BCC / LDY #$04 - capped at 4, and $4A starts at 1 - then LDA $FD4A,Y ($FD18) -> $05A8, slot 0's attack: 1 2 3 5. Then $FD44: LDA $FD4F,Y -> $0698 with Y = 0 or 2 (from $0590 below or above 5) plus 1 when $30 bit 6 is set: 03 05 41 06. 4 + 4 bytes, ending on the code at $FD53. This also confirms that $4A is 1-4.

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): flickering arrival (`$FD53`, slot `$C009`)
regions.description: `$0788,X` zero returns to the handler. Otherwise the handler is abandoned (two return addresses dropped), `$0788` counts down, and only the odd values draw (`JMP $CBFC`): the 40-60 frame flicker.

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): add life (`$FD67`, slot `$C00C`)
regions.description: `$48` += A, capped at `$FF` and at `$47`.

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): the selected weapon (`$FD77`, slot `$C135`)
regions.description: `$45` := 0; `$3D` := the level of weapon `$3C` (via `$E498`; 0 for none); `$3B` := `$FDCA[$3C]` (the highest slot below the A weapon's objects); weapon 0 or level 0, or the Eraser (12: the stock `$04AF`) goes straight to `$3E`; else **the chip cost `$45` := `$FDD3[3 x weapon + level]`**.

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): uses left (`$FDAA`, slot `$C138`)
regions.description: `$3E` := chips / cost: 255 if the chips' high byte is at least the cost; a cost with bit 7 halves both before the 16-bit divide (`$F9BA`).

regions.name: Per-selection value copied to $3B
regions.description: $FD77 does LDA $FDCA,Y / STA $3B with Y = the selected weapon $3C, 0-12: thirteen bytes. What $3B controls is NOT established.

regions.name: Use-chip cost: 11 weapons x 3 levels
regions.description: $FD77 computes Y = 3 * $3C + $3D and reads $FDD3,Y into $45, the chips one use costs - the number the status screen prints after 'USE CHIP'. $3C is 1-11 here (0 and 12 skip the read) and the level $3D is 1-3, so Y runs 4-36 and the bytes read are $FDD7-$FDF7: 33, ending exactly where the code at $FDF8 begins and starting exactly after the 13-byte table at $FDCA. Weapon 12 has no cost row - its count comes from $04AF instead. The costs rise steeply with level, e.g. 1, 3, 10 and 1, 5, 40.

regions.name: SHIP STATS, CHIPS, WEAPON COST (bank 7 `$FCE7-$FDC9`, `$FDF8`): set up a beam piece (`$FDF8`, slot `$C13B`)
regions.description: A = a style record offset (3 n) into `$FE22`; Y = the new object: **metasprite `$0548` := byte 0, `$0638` := byte 1, `$0650` (the half-width) := byte 2; flags `$0620` and attribute `$0560` := 0, hit points `$FF`, attack 1**.

regions.name: Beam style records: 9 x [metasprite][`$0638`][half-width]
regions.description: `00 40 03 | 1A 60 08 | 17 F0 18 | 00 20 02 | 00 40 02 | 00 60 02 | 1A F0 08 | 00 F0 08 | 00 10 08`, read at `$FE22 + 3n` (n = 0 Hyper Laser level 1, 1 level 2, 2 level 3; 3, 4, 5 Optomon's three beams; 6 Clawbot; 7 Eyegore; 8 the bank 6 `$6A`/`$69` beams): the beam's picture, its `$0638` (a length parameter) and its half-width in pixels. The earlier generated cards `$FE22`, `$FE23` and `$FE24` were this table's columns.

regions.name: BEAM AND SHOT HELPERS (bank 7 `$FE3D-$FEDD`): make a beam piece (`$FE3D`, slot `$C13E`)
regions.description: `LDA #$22 / JSR $FA4B`: a type-`$22` child of object X in slot Y. It gets `$06C8,Y` := `$17`, `$05D8,Y` := `$16` (the two halves of the style-record pointer the caller built from `$FE22`), **`$0668,Y` := X (its parent slot) and `$0680,Y` := the parent's type** - the two fields the beam machine `$FB76` reads.

regions.name: BEAM AND SHOT HELPERS (bank 7 `$FE3D-$FEDD`): store the beam end (`$FE57`, slot `$C141`)
BEAM AND SHOT HELPERS (bank 7 `$FE3D-$FEDD`): re-aim countdown (`$FE63`, slot `$C144`)
regions.description: `$0680,X` = the number of re-aims left (0 returns with carry clear), `$0668,X` the countdown: at 0 it is reloaded from A, the object aims at the player (`$F85D`) and `$0680` is decremented; carry set means it just re-aimed.

regions.name: BEAM AND SHOT HELPERS (bank 7 `$FE3D-$FEDD`): zero the velocity (`$FE79`, slot `$C147`)
regions.description: `$05C0`, `$05D8`, `$05F0`, `$0608` := 0 (the y and x speeds and their fractions).

regions.name: Difficulty scaling (slot $C162): start
regions.description: ENEMY STAT SCALING BY AREA (slot `$C162`, called by most enemy handlers when they are made): `$50` is the labyrinth area, or in a corridor the corridor folded onto 1-10. `$50` = 0 goes to the three halvings; otherwise A := (`$50` + 1) / 2 (1 for areas 1-2, 2 for 3-4, 3 for 5-6, 4 for 7-8, 5 for 9-10).

regions.name: Difficulty scaling: halve
regions.description: Y := A (0 for area 0), then three minus A times: attack `$05A8,X` and hit points `$0590,X` are halved (never below 1). A = 3 returns unchanged (`$FEB0`); A of 4 or more goes to the doubling. RUN: from (64, 64): area 0 -> 8, areas 1-2 -> 16, areas 3-4 -> 32.

regions.name: Difficulty scaling: double
regions.description: A - 3 times: attack and hit points are doubled, capped at `$FF`. RUN: areas 5-6 -> 64 (unchanged), 7-8 -> 128, 9-10 -> 255 (4 times, capped). So an enemy's strength runs 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4 times its table value across the areas.

regions.name: BEAM AND SHOT HELPERS (bank 7 `$FE3D-$FEDD`): spend the shot (`$FECC`, slot `$C168`)
regions.description: Sound `$21`; the shot in slot Y loses `$14` + 1 (the carry is clear after the sound call) = **21 hit points** (floor 0) and the call returns. Used where a part cannot be hurt: the spore `$72`, It's arms.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): reset (`$FEDE`, slot `$C000`, the RESET vector)
regions.description: `SEI / CLD`, the stack `$FF`.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): PPU off
regions.description: PPUCTRL := `$30`.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): wait for three vblanks
regions.description: `LDX #3`; three times: poll PPUSTATUS bit 7 (the PPU needs its warm-up).

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): APU
regions.description: `$4015` := `$0F` (four channels on, DMC off), `$4017` := `$C0` (no frame IRQ).

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): clear the RAM
regions.description: `$0000-$07FF` := 0 (X from 0 to 255 and all eight pages).

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): PPU set-up
regions.description: `$FF` := `$30` through `$D4E7` (PPUCTRL: 8 x 16 sprites, background from table 1, NMI off) and `$FE` := 6 through `$D4CF` (PPUMASK: left column shown, rendering off).

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): check the mapper
regions.description: Y from 6 down to 0: switch to bank Y and compare `$BFFF` with Y; a match goes on. **A mismatch loads a colour from `$FF3A,Y` into the backdrop `$0180`, forces the palette out (`$DED2`) and spins at `JMP $FF37` for ever** - the colour says which bank failed.

regions.name: Bank-check failure codes
regions.description: Seven bytes, $0F $01 $06 $14 $0A $31 $28, one per switchable PRG bank. Read by LDA $FF3A,Y at $FF2E, the failure arm of the boot-time bank check described on the bank identity bytes, with Y holding the bank that did not answer correctly. The value is stored to $0180 and $DED2 is called, after which $FF37 spins forever. Both edges of the region are pinned by structure and not argued: the byte before is the last byte of JMP $FF37 at $FF37-$FF39, the byte after is the DEY at $FF41 that the success path branches to, and Y is bounded to 0-6 by the LDY #$06 at $FF23 and the BPL at $FF42 - so the reader accounts for exactly these seven bytes and no others. NOT ESTABLISHED: what the values mean. They are not the bank numbers and they are not consecutive. The obvious lead is that they are tile or character codes for something drawn on screen, which is a question about $DED2 and about $0180, and neither has been traced yet.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): next bank
regions.description: `DEY / BPL $FF25`.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): bank 6 reset
regions.description: Bank 6 (`$D762`), `JSR $800F` (bank 6 reset init `$8015`: queue, sound init, DMC timer, score, zero page).

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): the title (`$FF4A`, slot `$C14D`)
regions.description: Stack reset; bank 0 (`$D714`), `JSR $800C` (bank 0 `$8332`: the sound-test check and the title screen and its menu); `$2F` zero goes on to `$FF5D`, else (the title's second item) bank 3 (`$D73B`) `JSR $800C`: the password screen, and then on.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): start the game (`$FF5D`, slot `$C150`)
regions.description: Stack reset, sound `$1F` (stop the music), the fade out (`$EDD1`), rendering off (`$D4C1`), bank 0 `JSR $8003` (the game set-up `$805B`), `JSR $E110` (the HUD's score row), bank 6, `JSR $CDA2` (the sprite allocator's start).

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): the main loop
regions.description: `JSR $E655` (the stage step), `LDY #1 / JSR $FF8B` (one game-loop pass), `JSR $D76F` with `03 0E 80` (bank 3 `$800F`: the boss and miniboss routine `$917F`), and round again.

regions.name: Far-call argument at $FF85
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $FF82 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 3 $800F**. The stored word is $800E rather than $800F because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): loop jump
regions.description: `JMP $FF7A`.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): game-loop passes (`$FF8B`, slot `$C024`)
regions.description: X and Y saved. Y times: **the frame sync (`$DA9A`), the pads and pause (`$F493`), `JSR $D76F` with `06 FF 7F` (bank 6 `$8000`, the object loop),**

regions.name: Far-call argument at $FF98
regions.description: Three bytes of far-call argument following `JSR $D76F` at bank 7 $FF95 - bank number, then the target address minus one, little-endian. They select **bank 6 $8000**. The stored word is $7FFF rather than $8000 because $D790 pushes these two bytes as a fake return address and lets RTS add the one back; that is not an inference, it is what the four instructions at $D799-$D7A4 do. A far call is the one reference in this ROM that no grep for an operand will ever surface, so the target is recorded here where a reader will find it.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): game-loop passes, the rest
regions.description: the HUD (`$E0F9`) and the decompressor's share (`$DB52`); Y counts down; X and Y restored; `RTS`.

regions.name: Fill: 23 x $FF
regions.description: Between the end of the traced code at $FFA8 and the DMC sample at $FFC0. All $FF; no reader.

regions.name: DMC sample: 17 zero bytes (a timer, not a sound)
regions.description: Bank 6 $802A writes $4012 = $FF (sample address $C000 + $FF x 64 = $FFC0) and $4013 = $01 (length 1 x 16 + 1 = 17 bytes), with $4011 = $00. These are those 17 bytes, all zero, so the channel outputs silence; the point is the sample-finished IRQ, which the handler at $DCF3 uses to time the raster split. $FFC0 is 64-byte aligned, as the DMC requires.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): wait Y frames (`$FFD1`, slot `$C021`)
regions.description: `$2B` := 0 and the frame sync (`$DA9A`) Y times.

regions.name: RESET AND MAIN LOOP (bank 7 `$FEDE-$FFDF`): area music (`$FFDC`, slot `$C15F`)
regions.description: Plays the song `$EF16[$50]` (the labyrinth's music by area).

regions.name: Fill: 14 x $FF
regions.description: Between the traced code ending at $FFE3 and the bank-switch table at $FFF2. All $FF; no reader.

regions.name: PRG bank table (bus-conflict-free switch values)
regions.description: Eight bytes, $80 through $87, one per PRG bank, at $FFF2-$FFF9. This is the standard UxROM answer to bus conflicts. On these boards a write to $8000-$FFFF is ANDed with whatever the ROM is driving at that address, so the only write that is guaranteed to land is one whose value already equals the ROM byte. The game therefore never writes a bank number out of thin air: it reads entry n of this table and writes the byte straight back where it came from, so the two agree by construction. The high bit is set in all eight values and is discarded - UxROM latches only as many low bits as it has banks, and with eight banks that is the low three - which is why $80+n selects bank n. Confirmed by the switching code and not by the shape of the table: $D79F-$D7A2 is LDA $FFF2,Y / STA $FFF2,Y with Y holding the bank number, $D70B-$D70E is the same pair, and seven more routines at $D719, $D726, $D733, $D740, $D74D, $D75A and $D767 do it with the address of one fixed entry. Both edges of the region are pinned by structure rather than argued: $FFF0-$FFF1 are $FF, and the byte after the eighth entry is the low half of the NMI vector. LEAD, not established: the eighth entry ($87, bank 7) exists, so the fixed bank can in principle also be selected into the $8000 window - but the seven fixed-address routines cover banks 0 to 6 only, and no call site has yet been found that hands the generic routine a 7.

fields.name: bank0
fields.description: Written to $FFF2 to select PRG bank 0 at $8000-$BFFF. Loaded and stored by $D719/$D71C.

fields.name: bank1
fields.description: Written to $FFF3 to select PRG bank 1. Loaded and stored by $D726/$D729.

fields.name: bank2
fields.description: Written to $FFF4 to select PRG bank 2. Loaded and stored by $D733/$D736.

fields.name: bank3
fields.description: Written to $FFF5 to select PRG bank 3. Loaded and stored by $D740/$D743.

fields.name: bank4
fields.description: Written to $FFF6 to select PRG bank 4. Loaded and stored by $D74D/$D750.

fields.name: bank5
fields.description: Written to $FFF7 to select PRG bank 5. Loaded and stored by $D75A/$D75D.

fields.name: bank6
fields.description: Written to $FFF8 to select PRG bank 6. Loaded and stored by $D767/$D76A.

fields.name: bank7
fields.description: Would select PRG bank 7 into the $8000 window. No fixed-address routine uses this entry; it is reachable only through the indexed pair at $D70B/$D70E or $D79F/$D7A2, and no call site passing a 7 has been found yet. Whether the entry is live or vestigial is NOT established.

regions.name: 6502 interrupt vectors
regions.description: The three 16-bit little-endian addresses the 6502 fetches on NMI, on reset and on IRQ/BRK. Their position is fixed by the CPU, not chosen: $FFFA, $FFFC and $FFFE are the last six bytes of the address space, which is why they are the last six bytes of the file. All three point into bank 7, which is the only place they could usefully point on a UxROM board - $C000-$FFFF is the one window that is guaranteed to hold the same bytes whatever the bank register says. Each target was disassembled and each decodes as the handler its vector names, which is the check that makes these six bytes a confirmed claim rather than a convention: a wrong pair here would still be a legal address, and only the code at the other end can say it is the right one.

fields.name: nmi
fields.description: NMI vector = $DC75, taken once per frame at the start of vblank. The target is a vblank handler and decodes as one: PHA / TXA / PHA / TYA / PHA saves the registers, then $FE is masked with #$E7 and written to PPUMASK, a frame counter at $2B is incremented, PPUSTATUS is read into $26, and OAM DMA is kicked off by writing $00 to OAMADDR and $02 to OAMDMA - so sprite memory is staged in CPU page 2. NOT YET ESTABLISHED: whether this handler ever dispatches through a vector held in RAM. The playbook warns that a RAM vector is where a static trace stalls and that it can hide a quarter of a bank, so that question has to be answered before any coverage figure for bank 7 means anything.

fields.name: reset
fields.description: RESET vector = $FEDE, taken at power-on and on the console's reset button. The target is a textbook 6502 power-on sequence and decodes as one: SEI / CLD / LDX #$FF / TXS, then $30 to PPUCTRL, then PPUSTATUS polled until bit 7 clears three times over (the standard wait for the PPU to warm up), then $0F to APUSTATUS and $C0 to $4017, then a loop that clears all eight pages of $0000-$07FF with a single X index. The clear covers $0100-$01FF, so the stack is zeroed too - which is worth knowing before reading anything into stack contents in a savestate.

fields.name: irq
fields.description: IRQ/BRK vector = $DCF3. This one is not a stub, and that is worth saying out loud because on many cartridges it is: mapper 2 has no scanline counter, so the only interrupt source on this board is the APU - the DMC sample-finished IRQ or the frame counter. The handler saves A, writes $0F to APUSTATUS, reads the frame counter at $2B, and then polls PPUSTATUS bit 6 (the sprite 0 hit flag) with BIT/BVS in a short loop before reloading DMC_FREQ from $05 and returning with RTI. So the same handler is doing sample housekeeping and mid-frame timing. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of the two interrupt sources is actually enabled, and when. That is a question about writes to $4010 and $4017 elsewhere in the ROM, and those have not been enumerated.
